ACC106.title: Accounting Principles 1
ACC106.description: This course is an introduction to financial accounting methods such as recording and book- keeping in the journal, ledger, and trial balance in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). This course is designed to help students apply the appropriate accounting treatment for both adjusting and closing operations. It also helps students in recording business transactions of merchandising companies, calculating cost of inventories, and illustrating internal control and bank reconciliation statement

ACC200.title: Accounting Principles 2
ACC200.description: This course introduces advanced accounting concepts to students, including different forms of ownership, cash flows statemen, financial analysis, accounting for manufacturing operations. The purpose of this course is to provide the students with the basis of accounting skills required in Business Administration to be used in the business environment for decision making

ACC301.title: Intermediate Accounting 1
ACC301.description: The main purpose of this course is to enhance the student’s knowledge of accounting concepts at a more advanced level. The emphasis is on the application of more advanced principles and alternative methods rather than routine accounting procedures. This course covers the underlying principles, procedures, and reporting requirements necessary to gain an understanding of both the preparation and the use of detailed financial statements. Topics include: the conceptual framework of financial accounting; financial statements preparation including the classified statement of financial position, the multiple-step income statement, and the statement of cash flows under IFRS considerations; as well as key issues related to the valuation and recording of cash, receivables, inventories, and plant assets

ACC303.title: Accounting Information Systems
ACC303.description: The purpose of this course is to provide students with analytical tools necessary to design, implement, maintain, and assess an accounting information system to support business processes and cycles. This course focuses on the use of information systems in the accounting process with an emphasis on computer systems, internal controls, fraud and ethics. Major topics also include the conception of dataflow diagrams, revenue, expenditure, production cycles and the extensible Business Reporting Language XBRL

ACC305.title: Governmental Accounting
ACC305.description: This course introduces students to characteristics and objectives financial reporting of governmental entities. It includes the principles of accounting and financial reporting for estate and local governments. It also consists of providing an overview of governmental operating statement and budgetary accounting system. The course helps students in preparing journal entries for transactions, capital projects and long-term liabilities as well as preparing government wide-financial statements and fund financial statements. The course presents principles, procedures, and disclosures applicable to UAE public sector organizations

ACC307.title: Intermediate Accounting 2
ACC307.description: This course is a continuation of Intermediate Accounting1, and is a closer look at the theories, principles and practices underlying financial statements. Emphasis is on the measurement, valuation and reporting of liabilities and stockholders’ equity and their effect on reported earnings. Topics covered include current and long-term liabilities, stockholders’ equity and retained earnings, dilutive securities, and earnings per share (EPS), investments, revenue recognition, leases, accounting changes and errors analysis and presentation and disclosure in financial reporting

ACC310.title: Taxation
ACC310.description: This course is an introduction to taxation with an emphasis on individuals and business entities. Topics include tax planning, elements of individual and business income tax and taxation in the UAE (VAT and corporate tax). It also consists of determining income, exclusions, deductions and computations of individuals and business income tax and tax credits. This course is designed to help students apply the appropriate tax accounting methods both tax consequences related with purchasing of assets, property dispositions and depreciation methods. Emphasis will be placed on transfer tax and wealth planning. The course provides insight of international taxation models of GCC, UK and USA

ACC401.title: Managerial Accounting
ACC401.description: This course is designed to expose students to the theory and practice of selecting and analyzing managerial and financial accounting information for internal use by managers for decision-making, planning, directing, and controlling purposes. Major topics include managerial accounting concepts, cost behavior, cost analysis, budgeting and profit planning, cost- volume profit analysis, measurement, and analysis of accounting data appropriate to managerial decision making, capital budgeting decision

ACC403.title: Cost Accounting
ACC403.description: This course exposes students to the basic concepts and practice of cost accounting System and their terminology with an emphasis on types of costs. It includes job order and process costing systems. It also introduces an overview of activity-based costing method. The course helps students in preparing flexible budget and variance analysis. The course presents the fundamental features of capacity analysis and inventory costing system

ACC405.title: Auditing
ACC405.description: This course is designed to provide the student with a basic understanding of all aspects of auditing. These include accepting and planning the audit, evaluating internal controls, verifying account balances and financial statement assertions, reporting on audited financial statements, as well as auditing standards, professional and personal ethical responsibilities of auditors

ACC413.title: Advanced Accounting
ACC413.description: The aim of this course is to critically examine advanced issues in financial accounting for business combinations, including the equity method of accounting for investments, consolidation of financial statements, intercompany transactions, and other related issues. The course also include accounting for partnerships, including formation, operations, termination, and liquidation

ACC415.title: Graduation Project
ACC415.description: This course provides an opportunity for students to employ academic tools and analysis techniques to research a project that is directly relevant to their majors and their future career. This course can be offered as a 3-credit hour course for students who wish to pursue only the classroom portion of this course and a 6-credit hour course for those who wish to combine research with an internship. The Graduation Project will include weekly classroom sessions for all students to engage in discussions related to idea generation, research techniques and data analysis. Students will also be required to attend several smaller group sessions in which they present their ideas and progress and receive feedback. Students may work individually or in teams and must deliver a case study or paper at the end of the course

ACC419.title: Internship
ACC419.description: The course requires students to complete a set number of hours in a private or public organization. Students may choose to undertake their internship in any area of business administration. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of Liwa College. Elective Courses

BAF301.title: Introduction to Financial Management
BAF301.description: This course is prepared to equip students with the fundamentals of financial management. It includes an overview of financial management, analysis of financial Statement, time value of money, risk and return, working capital management, financial statement analysis, sources of finance, and capital budgeting

BAF305.title: Corporate Finance
BAF305.description: This course is prepared to equip students with Introduction to Corporate Finance, the role of the financial manager, net Present Value and Investments, Risk, Return and Opportunity Costs, Capital Budgeting Analysis, Market Efficiency, Corporate Financing include Patterns of corporate financing, Debt and equity issuance, Private placements, Payout policies, Dividends, Stock repurchases, Deciding on a payout policy

BAF307.title: Investment
BAF307.description: This course is an introduction to the fundamental principles of investment management. The course focuses on risk and return analysis across different securities as well as performance evaluation, style analysis, and the behavior of money management professionals in the investment industry. Topics covered include portfolio theory and diversification, mean variance analysis, the efficient market hypothesis and capital asset pricing models

BAF311.title: Risk Management & Insurance
BAF311.description: This course provides an introduction to the field of risk management and insurance. Topics covered include public and private insurers, insurance contracts, insurer operations, insurance markets and the global insurance industry, as well as life and health risk management and insurance, personal property and liability risk management and insurance and commercial liability risk management and insurance

BAF403.title: Financial Institutions & Markets
BAF403.description: This course provides the learner with an overview on the operation of the financial system within the framework of modern economic and finance theory. It focuses on financial institutions and their role in financial intermediation, financial instruments, and pricing in primary and secondary, stock markets. It also focuses on the share price analysis in global markets and forward and future markets in financial risk management

BAF413.title: Financial Derivatives
BAF413.description: This course is a basic introduction to futures, options and other financial derivatives and will discuss the characteristics of different types of derivatives and how they are traded. The main topics include forwards, futures, swaps, options, binomial options pricing, the Black-Scholes formula, and financial engineering for hedging and risk management. The course will also cover the volatility of derivatives and their increasing importance in financial markets. BBA in Banking and Finance – Concentration Finance Major Courses

This course can be offered as a 3-credit hour course for students who wish to pursue only the classroom portion of this course and a 6-credit hour course for those who wish to combine research with an internship. Students will also be required to attend several smaller group sessions in which they present their ideas and progress and receive feedback. BAF421.title: Commercial Banking Management
BAF421.description: This course focuses on Commercial Bank Management. Major topics include the financial services offered by banks and the Impact of Government Policies and Regulation on them. The course analysis the functional areas of banking including the management of deposits, loans and Consumer and Real Estate Lending

BIM200.title: Linear Algebra
BIM200.description: This course is an introduction to Linear Algebra and some of its applications. The aim is to teach the fundamentals of linear algebra in a way that illustrates their relevance to business mathematics applications. An Introduction to Matrices and Systems of Linear Equations are given with other topics such as Determinants, Linear Transformations, Eigenvectors and Eigen values. Techniques and application of business mathematics of linear algebra for finance sciences, management, and economics

BIM301.title: Maintenance Management
BIM301.description: This course represents a deep comprehensive study of operations and activities of maintenance and the means and methods to manage a maintenance department in an industrial plant. This course contains an overview of maintenance functions and activities with a study of the different maintenance types and problem-solving methods of maintenance issues, including Design, Analysis, Evaluation and Control tools for Maintenance Management

BIM302.title: Operations Planning and Scheduling
BIM302.description: This course introduces the functional area of production and operations management as practiced in manufacturing industries and the services sector. It includes decision-making, just-in-time systems, forecasting, aggregate planning, inventory management, materials requirements planning (MRP), and operations scheduling

BIM303.title: Optimizing and Modeling
BIM303.description: This course introduces concepts and techniques of operations research and management science for the modeling and solution of business decision problems. It gives broad coverage to the formulation of optimization models. The models specifically covered are integer programming, Markov chain, queuing theories, optimization algorithms. Emphasis is placed on the process of analyzing business scenarios and formulating models that address appropriate business decision problems

BIM401.title: Logistics & Supply Chain Management
BIM401.description: This subject is a survey of the fundamental analytic tools, approaches, and techniques which are useful in the design and operation of logistics systems and integrated supply chains. The material is taught from a managerial perspective, with an emphasis on where and how specific tools can be used to improve the overall performance and reduce the total cost of a supply chain. We place a strong emphasis on the development and use of fundamental models to illustrate the underlying concepts involved in both intra and inter-company logistics operations

BIM402.title: Lean Management & Six Sigma
BIM402.description: This course will provide the student with an introduction to lean production describing the background behind its development and how evaluations and assessments of production systems are performed. Lean production tools and techniques will be described and, in some cases, demonstrated in simulation exercises. Examples of applications in manufacturing and business processes will be presented

BIM403.title: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Systems
BIM403.description: This course will introduce students to enterprise systems and show how organizations use enterprise systems to run their operations more efficiently and effectively. They will learn about the critical success factors and implementation strategies that lead to enterprise system success, and about the informational, knowledge, and decision-making opportunities afforded by enterprise systems. The course will examine typical Enterprise Systems modules: materials management, supply chain management, customer relationship management, financials, projects and human resource management. Enterprise systems use a single database to integrate business transactions along and between processes, leading to benefits such as efficient and error-free workflows plus accounting, management reporting and improved decision making. The course will incorporate a laboratory component using SAP software

BIM410.title: Decision Science
BIM410.description: This course deals with decision making within a managerial context. It encompasses several systematic approaches to making decisions in problems often encountered by managers. In today’s business world, problems are too complex to rely simply on intuition and common sense. Quantitative decision tools such as management science and statistics allow decision makers to base decisions on data-driven and scientific methods. This course prepares students to describe, gather and analyze business data, and to use statistical and management science tools to make effective business decisions in operations, finance, marketing, management, and new product development

BIM412.title: Risk Management
BIM412.description: This course will examine the way in which business and society make an assessment of control and transfer risk. It is designed for the student with no previous knowledge of risk management. The goal of this course is to engage students in active discovery of risk management principles. Students will be prepared to function in a business environment, developing an awareness of the challenges, the tools, and the process of designing and implementing a risk management program

BIM415.title: Graduation Project

This course can be offered as a 3-credit hour course for students who wish to pursue only the classroom portion of this course and a 6-credit hour course for those who wish to combine research with an internship. The Graduation Project will include weekly classroom sessions for all students to engage in discussions related to idea generation, research techniques and data analysis. Students will also be required to attend several smaller group sessions in which they present their ideas and progress and receive feedback. BIM419.title: Internship
BIM419.description: The course requires students to complete a set number of hours in a private or public organization. Students may choose to undertake their internship in any area of business administration. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of Liwa University

BIT201.title: Introduction to Computer Programming
BIT201.description: Introduction to Computer Programming (ICP) is an introductory course designed to provide students with fundamental knowledge and skills in computer programming. The course covers key programming concepts, including problem-solving techniques, algorithm development, pseudocode, flowcharts, programming syntax, variables, data types, control structures, loops, arrays and functions. Students will build practical skills and explore how programming can support real-world and sustainability-focused solutions

BIT203.title: Management Information Systems
BIT203.description: This course is designed to introduce the Management Information systems concepts within the context of the business environment. It provides comprehensive and integrative coverage of essential new information technologies and their impact on business models and managerial decision-making. The course provides an integrated framework by showing how information systems are composed of management, organization, and technology elements

BIT205.title: Object-Oriented Programming
BIT205.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of Object- Oriented Programming (OOP) using the Java programming language. It covers essential OOP principles such as classes, objects, encapsulation, method overloading and overriding, static methods, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, and interfaces. Students will also explore input/output (I/O) operations using Java streams and learn how to connect and interact with relational databases using JDBC. In addition, the course teaches good practices in Graphical User Interface (GUI) development and emphasizes building real-world applications using a modular, object-oriented approach. Students are encouraged to develop solutions that contribute to sustainability and responsible digital innovation

BIT207.title: Introduction to Web Development
BIT207.description: This course is an introduction to Web Development using HTML language. It covers the following elements: Hypertext Markup Language (HTML), Cascading Style Sheets for creating web- formed Web pages that are compliant with current Web standards and how to publish students’ Web sites. In addition, this course covers the application of JavaScript and DHTML as client-side programming. Students will learn the best practices for sustainable web design, such as optimizing images and scripts, minimizing resource usage, and ensuring accessibility and usability

BIT305.title: Database Management Systems
BIT305.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of database systems, including database architecture, data models, and system components. It emphasizes the design of efficient relational databases using ER diagrams and their conversion into optimized schemas. Students will learn various normalization techniques to ensure data integrity, minimize redundancy, and support sustainable data storage. The course also provides a solid foundation in relational algebra and hands-on experience in SQL programming

BIT405.title: Business Intelligence
BIT405.description: This course illustrates the applicability of Business Intelligence (BI) in the development of successful business models. It investigates the role of data mining for BI in an organization. Students will first learn appropriate tools and techniques for data pre-processing and data exploration. Then, they will explore and apply some supervised and unsupervised data mining techniques to create valuable strategies and make wiser business decisions

BIT407.title: Object-Oriented Systems Analysis and Design
BIT407.description: This course introduces the principles and design techniques of object-oriented development approaches. It focuses on the process of developing information systems using object-oriented system analysis and design techniques based on the Unified Modeling Language (UML). Students will learn key concepts and methods used in the object-oriented system development process, including problem identification, application of object- oriented concepts and tools in problem solving, data gathering, modeling, analysis, project management, and design. The course also covers UML diagrams, validation techniques to assess model quality, and methods to ensure system requirements are met. Additionally, sustainable application design principles are emphasized to create reliable, long-term solutions

BIT413.title: Data Communication and Networking
BIT413.description: In this course students are going to be introduced to the basic computer network concepts and elements. Students will be taught the characteristics of network models, topologies, network devices, data transmission, and communication protocols going through more detail about IP addressing. Students will be introduced to network simulation tools to apply their theoretical knowledge to practical aspects. This course will also explore the concept of basic network data security, privacy, and sustainable networks

BIT415.title: Graduation Project
BIT415.description: This course offers students a unique opportunity to apply their learning about business technology and the entire software development lifecycle, from business needs to deployment. It amplifies classroom instruction about IT project planning and implementation. The Graduation Project will include weekly classroom sessions for all students to engage in discussions related to idea generation, research techniques and data analysis. Students will also be required to attend several smaller group sessions in which they present their ideas and progress and receive feedback. Students may work individually or in teams and must deliver a complete product (Application, website, planning designs, etc.) at the end of the course

BIT417.title: Advanced Web Development
BIT417.description: This course provides practical knowledge for designing and developing web-based applications using modern web development techniques. It focuses on HTML, CSS, and dynamic web content through interactive web technologies. Students will learn how to build dynamic web applications that integrate with databases. Throughout the course, students will work with advanced web techniques and technologies to develop a dynamic web application, including client-side tools, server-side technologies, and database connectivity. The course also introduces the concept of sustainable web design, emphasizing efficient coding practices and environmental considerations in web development

BIT419.title: Internship
BIT419.description: The course requires students to complete a set number of hours in a private or public organization. Students may choose to undertake their internship in any area of business administration. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of Liwa University. Elective Courses

BIT422.title: Advanced Database Management System
BIT422.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of sustainable database design and application development. It covers the implementation of both basic and advanced SQL queries optimized for efficiency and performance. The course emphasizes the development of database applications using PL/SQL and the creation of essential database objects, including views, triggers, procedures, functions, and packages. Key database management system (DBMS) concepts such as transaction processing, concurrency control, and recovery are explored to ensure data integrity, consistency, and reliability. Additionally, the design and development of user-friendly graphical interfaces using forms and reports are covered

BIT430.title: Information Security
BIT430.description: This course provides a foundational understanding of information and network security principles. It introduces key security concepts, terminology, and models essential for recognizing and addressing modern security challenges. Further, it explores various types of threats, including network attacks, computer-based attacks, and social engineering techniques. The course covers basic cryptographic methods, server vulnerabilities, and both wired and wireless network security infrastructure. Emphasis is placed on authentication mechanisms, vulnerability assessments, and the design and implementation of sustainable security solutions for stand-alone and networked systems

BMS110.title: Medical Terminology
BMS110.description: This course introduces students to the language of medicine, were gain of understanding several terms: prefixes, suffixes, and word roots are valuable to build and analyze medical words and terms associated with the body as a whole. Accordingly, student will define, interpret, and pronounce medical terms relating to structure and function, pathology, diagnosis, clinical procedures, oncology, and pharmacology. In addition to medical terms, common abbreviations applicable to each system will be interpreted

BMS121.title: Human Anatomy
BMS121.description: This course is designed to give the student a sound background in structure of the human body as a whole. Anatomy is the most fundamental of all medical sciences. It provides the basic framework of terminology and vocabulary used in all descriptions and communications about the body. The course will describe the structure, composition, and functions of the organ systems of the human body and how the organ systems function and interrelate. The course will also describe how humans adapt through their anatomical design

BMS122.title: Biochemistry
BMS122.description: This course is designed to provide the students with knowledge of the functions and mechanisms of various parts and organs of the human body. In addition, the course introduces the students to the integrity of the body systems as a whole in order to recognize the physiological changes that occur within the human body and how the body systems work. Students cover the topics of body mechanism, basic chemistry, function of the human body such as, cells and tissues, skin and body membranes, skeletal system, muscular system, nervous system with special senses, and the function of endocrine system, circulatory system with blood, body defenses, respiratory system, digestive system including body metabolism, urinary system, and a unit on human body reproduction. Course code: BMS 123 In this course, students are introduced to the general principles of biochemistry while linking them back to the physiological conditions of an organism. There are several topics designed into this course, relationship of biochemistry to the physiology of an organism, relationship of bioenergetics to the physiological state, regulation of rates through the metabolic pathways, and relationship of enzyme structure to catalysis and regulation. Description of the chemistry underlying most of the metabolic reaction’s role of DNA, RNA, and protein synthesis in the observed physiologic state Role of DNA in inheritance and genetic manipulation and gene therapy Students will know the basic information related to the following terms: saccharides, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids. In addition, enzymes, vitamins and how they work in the human body. Biochemistry also introduces essential information related to chemical combinations, biomaterials, classification, chemical structure, reactions and how the human body metabolizes such bio molecules

BMS124.title: Introduction to Microbiology
BMS124.description: This course is designed to provide an extensive overview of the microbial structure, functioning, and diversity of microorganisms, growth and pathogenesis and immunology are presented with important bacterial, viral, parasitic and mycotic infections discussed from the standpoint of aetiology, epidemiology, and pathogenesis and laboratory diagnosis. The Topics include microbial cell structure and function, metabolism, microbial genetics, and the role of microorganisms in disease, the environment and other selected areas

BMS410.title: General Pharmacology and Toxicology
BMS410.description: The goal of this course is to develop an understanding of the causes and mechanisms of human diseases and associated alterations of structure and function of tissues. This involves first, the general pathology during which cell injury, adaptation, cell death, repair, inflammation, and neoplasia are introduced. Then, diseases and tumors of general interest affecting different body systems such as immune system, digestive, respiratory and cardiovascular system are studied. Course code: BMS 411 This course is designed as an introduction to pharmacology and toxicology and deals with pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, clinical/therapeutic uses and toxicology of drugs, Pharmacology is broadly defined as the effect of drugs and chemicals on living organisms. It gives specific information concerning cardiopulmonary, vascular, central and peripheral nervous system, and antimicrobial drug classifications as well as common examples in each category. With each classification of drugs covered, their mode of action, their clinical effects and side effects will be emphasized. Core Major Courses

BS311.title: Cross Cultural Management
BS311.description: This course provides an overview of international organizational behavior and human resource issues and practices in multi- national organizations. Topics covered include understanding the effects of culture on attitudes and behavior, organizational issues such as structures, systems and technology, and human resource issues such as teamwork, leadership and negotiation, as well as different approaches for effective cross-cultural management

BSC120.title: Physics for Health Sciences
BSC120.description: This course is designed to introduce the physics of units of forces, energy changes in the body, heat loss from the body, and breathing mechanism. It helps the students acquire knowledge about electric signals of the body, general properties of sound in the body as a drum (percussion in medicine) and vision defects and corrections. Moreover, this course introduces light, vision, sound and atomic excitation

BSC121.title: Chemistry for Health Sciences
BSC121.description: This course will introduce basic theoretical principles of modern chemistry, integrated with descriptive and practical aspects. Topics discussed include stoichiometry, atomic theory and the structure of matter, the Periodic Table, chemical bonding, kinetic-molecular theory and the states of matter; gas laws, solutions, oxidation-reduction, acid-base systems, and thermochemistry. Emphasis is on both qualitative and quantitative aspects of chemistry. Laboratory sessions are designed to complement and supplement theoretical concepts presented in lectures and to develop skills in laboratory technique, observation and data analysis

BSC122.title: Biology for Health Sciences
BSC122.description: This course will introduce students to basic aspects of human biology. It commences with a general introduction to life, its chemical and biological basis, and the meaning of its unity and diversity. Cells, as the building blocks of living matter, will be discussed at length in terms of their structure, function, classification, physiology, genetics, and reproduction. Moving up the biological hierarchy, tissues constituting the human body will be discussed at length. Higher levels of organization like organs and organ systems will also be addressed in some detail

BSC220.title: Biostatistics
BSC220.description: This course aims to provide students the skills needed to analyze medical literature by understanding the fields of biostatistics such as data types, observational studies, inferential statistics, regression techniques, evaluating a cohort study and determinants of health. The course emphasizes principles of statistical reasoning, underlying assumptions and hypotheses, and interpretation of results. Topics covered include descriptive statistics, graphical displays of data, introduction to probability, expectations and variance of random variables, confidence intervals and tests for means, differences of means, proportions, differences of proportions, chi-square tests for categorical variables, regression and multiple regressions and an introduction to analysis of variance. Statistical software will be used to supplement manual calculation. Perform inference on population means and proportions via sample data; statistical hypothesis testing and its application to group comparisons; issues of power and sample size in study designs; and random sample and other study types. While there are some formulae and computational elements to the course, the emphasis is on interpretation and concepts

BSC221.title: Research Methods for Health Sciences
BSC221.description: This is an introductory course to clinical research providing a comprehensive introduction to research methodology, including its theoretical foundation, fundamental protocols, and evidence- based practice (EBP). The course offers a practical approach to the identification, organization, and critique of such evidence. Also, in this course, students learn about research methodologies, which include pure and applied research, and interactive process of research writing. The distinction between quantitative, qualitative, and mixed method approaches is emphasized in this course. The course also teaches students how to review literature and to write a research proposal. Basic Medical Science Courses for all Medical Programs

BUS100.title: Introduction to Management
BUS100.description: This course aims to introduce students with knowledge of the principles, functions and techniques of management to gain a solid background in business organization and management. Essential topics examined in this course include management functions, decision-making, motivation, communication. Special attention is paid to the cultural and regional context of business organizations. This course expected to serve as a foundation for other courses in business

BUS201.title: Microeconomics
BUS201.description: This course is an introductory course in economic theory and applications. It will familiarize the students with the basic principles of microeconomics. Topics that will be covered include behavior of households and firms, consumption possibilities & preferences, production functions and market structures

BUS203.title: Organizational Behavior
BUS203.description: This course examines the complex relationships among individuals, groups, organizations, and society. It emphasizes a dynamic systems approach to understanding and facilitating work relationships through the study of the interaction of individual needs, abilities, and traits with organizational goals and structures. Some of the contemporary organizational issues included in this course are individual and group dynamics, motivation and performance, leadership, power, organizational culture, organizational change, and development

BUS301.title: Macroeconomics
BUS301.description: This course provides an understanding of the role and methodology of economics, components of the economy, roles of government and central bank in the economy through fiscal policy, monetary policy, and system. This course also covers macroeconomic indicators (GDP, Inflation, and Unemployment), economic growth and the business cycle

BUS302.title: e-Business
BUS302.description: this course develops the student’s understanding of basic principles of e-business and ecommerce management, functions, technologies, and goals. The course covers e-business models, strategies, and applications with the explanation of most computer jargon and terminology relevant to e-commerce

BUS305.title: Business Law
BUS305.description: This course provides a high-level overview of key business- related legal issues. Subjects covered include legal terminology and concepts, the elements of contracts, intellectual property law, employment law, and the legal relationships between buyers and sellers. In addition, there will be a focus on how these issues apply in the context of the legal environment in the UAE

BUS306.title: Quantitative Business Analysis
BUS306.description: This course provides a comprehensive survey of the main quantitative business techniques used in business analysis and decision making, in particular the application of mathematical and statistical models in the analysis of problems related to economic and administrative sciences. The main topic includes decision making analysis under uncertainty, regression analysis and hypothesis testing, forecasting techniques, linear programming models and network analysis

BUS307.title: Research Methods
BUS307.description: The course is designed to introduce students to qualitative and quantitative research methods, as well as commonly used statistical procedures in data analysis. Topics covered include the role of business research, scientific inquiry, the research process, proposal development, research design, hypothesis testing, primary and secondary data collection, statistical data analysis and presentation of research reports. The ethical issues of research design and data interpretation will also be discussed

BUS309.title: Operations Management
BUS309.description: This course provides a foundation in fundamental concepts, techniques and applications of contemporary production and operations management to serve as tools for improving quality, productivity and international competitiveness. It covers a selection of quantitative tools and techniques to aid in decision making and operations management setting. Topics such as forecasting, product and service development, capacity planning, process selection, facility planning, quality management and inventory management will be introduced. The concepts for designing, planning and improving manufacturing and service organizations will also be examined

BUS311.title: Cross Cultural Management
BUS311.description: This course provides an overview of international organizational behavior and human resource issues and practices in multi- national organizations. Topics covered include understanding the effects of culture on attitudes and behavior, organizational issues such as structures, systems and technology, and human resource issues such as teamwork, leadership and negotiation, as well as different approaches for effective cross-cultural management

BUS401.title: Quality Management
BUS401.description: This course is designed to provide students with an understanding of the principles, concepts, processes and procedures pertaining to the issue of total quality management. Topics covered include: the origins of the modern day quality movement, the philosophies and practices that serve as the theoretical knowledge for planning and implementing a total quality management (TQM) program, the principles that make up TQM, the implications and benefits of introducing TQM into an organization, and the tools and techniques that could be used to support an ongoing TQM program

BUS407.title: Project Management
BUS407.description: This course represents a deep comprehensive study of operations and activities of project and the means and methods to manage a project department in an any fields specially constructions. This course contains an overview of project functions and activities with a study of the different projects types and problem-solving methods of maintenance issues, including Design, Analysis, Evaluation and Control tools for Project Management. Bachelor of Business Administration in Industrial Management Major Courses

BUS409.title: Strategic Management
BUS409.description: This course is capstone course that attempts to addresses the main areas of strategic management process and assessment of how company’s strategy interacts with and guides within its external and internal environments. The focus of the course is on business unit and corporate-level strategy, strategy formulating, strategy implementation, and covering the overall strategic management process. Also, it examines how organizations can sustain competitive advantage and how corporate strategies can be implemented successfully. The course covers strategic implementation as its relation to strategic leadership, organizational structure, and culture. Case analyses and text material are employed to integrate student’s knowledge and improve strategic thinking skills

BUS411.title: Change Management
BUS411.description: This course introduces an overview of change situations, and the issues and methods associated with the management of change. The topics covered include identifying the need for change, planning and communicating change, strategies for implementing change, and overcoming resistance to change. Students will also examine the role of leadership and the competencies and skills required of individuals who initiate, manage, and are affected by change. BBA in Tourism and Hospitality Management Major Courses

BUS413.title: Leadership
BUS413.description: This course provides the basis for understanding what leadership is and what leaders do to be successful. This course will look at how successful leaders develop a vision for the future, align other behind their vision, and motivate them to achieve the vision. This course will review theories of leadership and analyze common strategies used by leaders, both effective and ineffective, as well as address moral and ethical responsibility of leadership

BUS415.title: Graduation Project
BUS415.description: This course provides an opportunity for students to employ the academic tools and analysis techniques to research a project that is directly relevant to their majors and their future career. This course can be offered as a 3 credit hour course for students who wish to pursue only the classroom portion of this course and a 6 credit hour course for those who wish to combine research with an internship. The Graduation Project will include weekly classroom sessions for all students to engage in discussions related to idea generation, research techniques and data analysis. Students will also be required to attend several smaller group sessions in which they present their ideas and progress, and receive feedback. Students may work individually or in teams and must deliver a case study or paper at the end of the course

BUS417.title: International Business Management
BUS417.description: This course is capstone course that attempts to addresses the main areas of strategic management process and assessment of how company’s strategy interacts with and guides within its external and internal environments. The focus of the course is on business unit and corporate-level strategy, strategy formulating, strategy implementation, and covering the overall strategic management process. Also, it examines how organizations can sustain competitive advantage and how corporate strategies can be implemented successfully. The course covers strategic implementation as its relation to strategic leadership, organizational structure, and culture. Case analyses and text material are employed to integrate student’s knowledge and improve strategic thinking skills. Major Courses

BUS419.title: Internship
BUS419.description: The course requires students to complete a set number of hours in a private or public organization. Students may choose to undertake their internship in any area of business administration. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of Liwa University. Elective Courses

BUS421.title: Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management
BUS421.description: This course provides an overview of critical issues faced in small business and entrepreneurship. This includes an overview of how strategic planning, operations, human resources and financial management issues are related to small business and entrepreneurs. This course also provides the student with a broad understanding of the basic issues in modern operations management in both manufacturing and service organizations. It focuses on the development of a strategic business plan and competitive business model for a small business or entrepreneurial venture. Special emphasis is placed on adapting business skills to the realistic needs of a small business owner and entrepreneur

CDM505.description: This course aims to enhance students' English language proficiency within the field of Media communication. It focuses on developing essential skills such as reading, writing, listening, and speaking. while deepening their understanding of language use in media contexts. Students will engage in analyzing and creating various media texts, including news articles, advertisements, blogs, podcasts, and social media content, preparing them to navigate both traditional and digital platforms effectively. The course emphasizes vocabulary development, critical thinking, media literacy, and practical communication skills. By the end of the course, students will be able to interpret, evaluate, and produce content that meets the evolving needs of the media industry

CDM701.prerequisites: Completion of 18 required credit hours, including the course CDM601

CGA101.title: Introduction to Visual Communication
CGA101.description: This course is an introductory visual communication design course that provides students with the practical knowledge and critical skills necessary to effectively consider visual design as an essential and inevitable component of their work as designers and visual advertising practitioners

CGA107.title: Introduction to Web Design
CGA107.description: This course examines the role of a website in various fields such as advertising, retail, education, news, and media, it introduces the basics of web design with HTML and CSS. The theoretical part of the course seeks to expound upon the significance of web design as a discipline, together with its main sociological implications. The course, however, places its main emphasis on the practical aspects relating to the topic/field, allowing students to acquire the skills necessary for the creation of basic, functional, and aesthetically pleasing websites. In this course, students will use a variety of design software to organize, create, publish, and manage a website. Course content considers usability issues in websites, and includes creating a variety of graphic elements, including video, animations, slideshow, rollover effects, backgrounds, and page images, to ensure that students can produce well-founded and interactive web pages and websites

CGA108.title: Desktop Publishing
CGA108.description: This course describes the main issues and technologies related to the use of appropriate graphic images within the context of printed media. It covers the role of printed media in various fields, the components of printed media, page layout considerations for printed media, desktop publishing technology, print media for specific markets, and the print process

CGA111.title: Storyboarding for Film & Animation
CGA111.description: To enable students to gain an understanding of the role of pre- production in the creation of time-dependent scenes. The course will also provide the students with an opportunity to practically realize a storyboard utilizing film language and shot description

CGA125.title: Digital Image Editing
CGA125.description: This course describes the concept of a bit-mapped image – resolution, bit depth, color channels and photo retouching describing the main uses of this technique. Covering digital image manipulation and editing techniques such as selection and masking specific areas of an image for protection, the course also looks at the major problem causes of photographic images & their correction. Several advanced manipulation techniques are discussed, and students are given the opportunity to see first- hand examples of image problems and correct these in practical sessions

CGA135.title: 2D Vector Graphics
CGA135.description: This course explains the concept of vector graphics, 2D vector graphic primitives, vector graphic attributes, operations on vector objects, creating complex objects by combining simple geometric primitives and rasterizing vector graphics for display at multiple resolutions

CGA145.title: 2D Animation
CGA145.description: This course explains the concepts of 2D animation – layout and compositing. It also covers cartoon animation, key frames, tweening and timelines & events within an animation

CGA155.title: 3D Modeling
CGA155.description: This course explains the 3D workspace, wireframe modeling and rendering. It also describes 3D graphic primitives, combining 3D primitives to form solid models, the camera in a 3D scene and simple shading concepts

CGA205.title: Typography and Art of Arabic Calligraphy
CGA205.description: In this course, students utilize computers in an advanced manner that explores more complex design problems. Students learn the discipline, function, and tradition of typography as it relates to visual verbal communications topics include historical revolution of typography, communication, legibility, languages sequence and information hierarchy. Students will learn the study of problem solving as well as the methodology of design thinking

CGA215.title: Digital Video Editing
CGA215.description: This course explains the digital video workflow – capture, scene identification, editing and final assembly. It also explains the benefits of digital video over analogue video, digital video formats, non-linear editing & edit decision lists and digital effects for video (transitions, wipes, fades, subtitles, and text)

CGA225.title: 3D Animation
CGA225.description: This course explains the 3D animation process – assembly, position and synchronization. It also covers manipulating the camera position over time, timelines for 3D scenes, simple scripting of 3D objects within a timeline and exporting a final movie as digital video

CGA235.title: The Human Form & Character Animation
CGA235.description: This course explains the human form – anatomy, skeleton, and muscle structure. It also explains the animation of human joins, forward an inverse kinematics in animation and the motion capture (Mocap) process & applying Mocap data to 3D models

CGA245.title: Principles of Texture, Materials & Lighting
CGA245.description: This course explains how to create textures from 2D raster and vector images, apply texture maps to 3D models – coloring a scene, create realistic material textures – bump mapping & displacement mapping, apply lighting in a 3D scene and apply shading – Gouraud, Phong, Ray-tracing & Radiosity

CGA255.title: Special Effects for Film
CGA255.description: This course explains the role and purpose of special effects, visual effects and the digital workflow – pre and postproduction considerations. It also explains the effects for specific applications – motion blur; lens effects; color and lighting effects. It also covers Overlays and chroma keying – recording action against a blue or green screen for the purpose of superimposing additional footage later on

CGA265.title: CGA Internship
CGA265.description: This course supervises work experience in the field of Computer Graphics and Animation. It offers important benefits to the graduating student, including the opportunity to earn credit while exploring a career in Computer Graphics and Animation and a chance to apply concepts learned in the Associate of Science Degree Program to real problems faced by firms. CIT100.title: Introduction to Information Technology
CIT100.description: This is an introductory personal computer applications course. It includes the operating system (MS Windows), word processing (MS Word), spreadsheets (MS Excel), and presentation manager (MS PowerPoint), database applications (MS Access)

CIT101.title: Introduction to Generative AI
CIT101.description: This course provides an introduction to essential software applications, including the operating system (MS Windows), word processing (MS Word), spreadsheets (MS Excel), and presentation management (MS PowerPoint). It also explores Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its practical applications across various industries. Designed for students without prior IT experience, the course emphasizes hands-on learning to develop practical skills. Students will gain an understanding of core concepts and learn to effectively use Generative AI tools. Key topics include crafting effective prompts, recognizing ethical considerations, and leveraging AI for creative problem-solving

CIT112.title: Introduction to Computer Programming
CIT112.description: Introduction to Computer Programming (ICP) is an introductory course designed to provide students with fundamental knowledge and skills in computer programming. The course covers key programming concepts, including problem-solving techniques, algorithm development, pseudocode, flowcharts, programming syntax, variables, data types, control structures, loops, arrays and functions. Students will build practical skills and explore how programming can support real-world and sustainability-focused solutions

CIT121.title: Introduction to Computer Architecture
CIT121.description: This course introduces the concept of computer as a set of hardware, software and data components integrated through different architecture models. The described hardware components include the processor, the memory and the input/output interfaces while the software components include the operating system, the utility software. The course presents data representation at the machine level and introduces the concepts of digital logic to solve sustainability related scenarios. In addition, the students will be given an overview of the evolution of computers and the associated technologies together with a presentation of future technological trends

CIT122.title: Introduction to Database Management Systems
CIT122.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of database systems, including database architecture, data models, and system components. It emphasizes the design of efficient relational databases using ER diagrams and their conversion into optimized schemas. Students will learn various normalization techniques to ensure data integrity, minimize redundancy, and support sustainable data storage. The course also provides a solid foundation in relational algebra and hands-on experience in SQL programming

CIT123.title: Computer Programming and Problem Solving
CIT123.description: This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of programming concepts and problem-solving techniques. Students will learn data structures, algorithms, and work with functions, modular design, libraries, handle files and exceptions, and manage dynamic data structures such as stacks, queues, linked lists, and trees. The course also emphasizes the role of programming in developing sustainable digital solutions

CIT231.title: Introduction to Computer Networks
CIT231.description: In this course students are going to be introduced to the basic computer network concepts and elements. Students will be taught the characteristics of network models, topologies, network devices, data transmission, and communication protocols going through more detail about IP addressing. Students will be introduced to network simulation tools to apply their theoretical knowledge to practical aspects. This course will also explore the concept of basic network data security, privacy, and sustainable networks

CIT232.title: Introduction to Operating Systems
CIT232.description: This course introduces the core concepts of operating systems and their functions such as memory management, process management and scheduling, handling concurrency and synchronization, file systems, input, and output device management. The course also covers the role of operating systems in management of security and privacy of users and network functions. Additionally, this course emphasizes the role of operating systems in promoting sustainable computing practices, including efficient resource utilization, energy-aware process scheduling, and support for green IT infrastructures. Industry-relevant examples such as mobile operating systems (Android), virtualization platforms (VMware, Docker), and cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure) will be introduced to help students relate OS concepts to real-world applications

CIT233.title: Software Development Process
CIT233.description: This course presents an introduction to the models, processes, and techniques used in developing software systems. It covers the entire life cycle of software systems, from project proposal and requirements analysis through design, development, testing, release, and maintenance. Students are introduced to industry-standard techniques such as fact-finding, software modeling, verification and validation, and system documentation. In alignment with the UAE's sustainability vision and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, this course incorporates eco-conscious software engineering principles. Students are exposed to the Software Carbon Intensity (SCI) Tool from the Green Software Foundation, enabling them to evaluate and reduce the environmental impact of their software designs

CIT234.title: Discrete Mathematics
CIT234.description: This course enables students to strengthen and increase their understanding of discrete mathematics with special emphasis on computer science applications. Binomial Coefficients, Combinations, Permutations, Combinatorial Proofs, Stars, and Bars will be covered in this course. Also concepts Arithmetic, Geometric Sequences, Polynomial Fitting, Solving Recurrence Relations, and Induction. Propositional Logic, Proofs, Graph Theory will be used to solve real-world problems. Additionally, Discrete Math for Sustainable Computing will be presented

CIT241.title: Network Security
CIT241.description: This course provides a foundational understanding of information and network security principles. It introduces key security concepts, terminology, and models essential for recognizing and addressing modern security challenges. Further, it explores various types of threats, including network attacks, computer-based attacks, and social engineering techniques. The course covers basic cryptographic methods, server vulnerabilities, and both wired and wireless network security infrastructure. Emphasis is placed on authentication mechanisms, vulnerability assessments, and the design and implementation of sustainable security solutions for stand-alone and networked systems

CIT242.title: Systems Analysis and Design
CIT242.description: This course introduces the principles and design techniques of object-oriented development approaches. It focuses on the process of developing information systems using object-oriented system analysis and design techniques based on the Unified Modeling Language (UML). Students will learn key concepts and methods used in the object-oriented system development process, including problem identification, application of object- oriented concepts and tools in problem solving, data gathering, modeling, analysis, project management, and design. The course also covers UML diagrams, validation techniques to assess model quality, and methods to ensure system requirements are met. Additionally, sustainable application design principles are emphasized to create reliable, long-term solutions

CIT243.title: Network Administration
CIT243.description: This course introduces concepts and technologies behind domain-based enterprise networks. The course covers installation, configuration and administration of enterprise network operating systems and protocols, and services such as active directory, group policies, data storage, backup and disaster recovery to the level required to effectively administer a secured domain-based enterprise networks for both traditional networks and green networks

CIT244.title: Database Programming
CIT244.description: This course presents mapping rules to convert conceptual and logical designs to physical designs. It also introduces the principles of normalization and denormalization taking into consideration various techniques which are applied to the different normal forms. The course also addresses the concepts of the PL/SQL procedural language including functions, procedures, cursors, packages, and triggers. In addition, this course discusses database problems and potential solutions and how to improve database performance, productivity, and portability through different integration patterns with DBMSs and programming languages in accordance with software application requirements

CIT352.title: Distributed Information Management
CIT352.description: This course provides a comprehensive examination of distributed information systems, which serve as the backbone of modern global organizations. It addresses the fundamental principles of distributed architecture, processes, communication protocols, consistency models, and fault tolerance mechanisms. Students will analyze components of distributed IT infrastructure, including operating systems, naming conventions, and communication frameworks. Particular emphasis is placed on the integration of sustainability principles, focusing on energy- efficient design, environmentally responsible computing practices, and the selection of sustainable cloud services. The course aims to equip students with both the theoretical foundation and practical insights required to design and manage distributed systems that are robust, scalable, and sustainable

CIT353.title: Web Development
CIT353.description: This course provides practical knowledge for designing and developing web-based applications using modern web development techniques. It focuses on HTML, CSS, and dynamic web content through interactive web technologies. Students will learn how to build dynamic web applications that integrate with databases. Throughout the course, students will work with advanced web techniques and technologies to develop a dynamic web application, including client-side tools, server-side technologies, and database connectivity. The course also introduces the concept of sustainable web design, emphasizing efficient coding practices and environmental considerations in web development

CIT354.title: Object-Oriented Programming
CIT354.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of Object- Oriented Programming (OOP) using the Java programming language. It covers essential OOP principles such as classes, objects, encapsulation, method overloading and overriding, static methods, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, and interfaces. Students will also explore input/output (I/O) operations using Java streams and learn how to connect and interact with relational databases using JDBC. In addition, the course teaches good practices in Graphical User Interface (GUI) development and emphasizes building real-world applications using a modular, object-oriented approach. Students are encouraged to develop solutions that contribute to sustainability and responsible digital innovation

CIT362.title: Information Security Management
CIT362.description: This course focuses on the managerial aspects of information security and assurance. Topics covered include access control models, information security governance, and information security program assessment and metrics. Coverage on the foundational and technical components of information security is included in reinforcing key concepts. The course includes up- to-date information on changes in the field, such as national and international laws and international standards like the ISO 27000 series, Risk Management, Security Mechanisms, and Blockchain concepts and applications. Sustainable security practices are emphasized to ensure long-term protection, efficiency, and responsible resource management

CIT365.title: Advanced Database Design
CIT365.description: This course offers an in-depth exploration of advanced database design, with a particular emphasis on data warehouse architecture and implementation using industry-relevant tools. Students will engage in conceptual, logical, and physical design stages while examining key topics such as big data management, database administration, and integration with web services. Practical skills will be developed through hands-on use of platforms such as MySQL, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server for relational databases, and Power BI for business intelligence and dashboard creation. The course also introduces NoSQL systems (e.g., MongoDB) and cloud-based environments (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure) to emphasize sustainable data storage and processing. Sustainable database design principles, including energy efficiency, optimized queries, and responsible cloud resource use are woven throughout the course to prepare students for building scalable, high-performance, and environmentally responsible data systems

CIT450.title: Machine Learning
CIT450.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of machine learning fundamentals, covering supervised and unsupervised learning techniques. Students will learn various algorithms and methodologies, including regression, classification, deep learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), and clustering. Advanced topics such as regularization and reinforcement learning are also explored. In addition, the course integrates sustainable AI practices, utilizing cloud platforms to optimize computational efficiency, reduce energy consumption, and promote responsible data management. Students will apply these techniques in real-world industry scenarios

CIT451.title: Computer Vision
CIT451.description: This course introduces students to the foundational concepts, algorithms, and practical tools in computer vision. Topics include image formation, processing, feature extraction, object detection, and image segmentation. Emphasis is placed on real- world applications using libraries such as OpenCV and deep learning frameworks. The course also explores how computer vision technologies contribute to sustainable development through applications in smart cities, environmental monitoring, and efficient resource management. Students will gain both theoretical understanding and hands-on experience through projects that align with sustainable innovation goals

CIT453.title: Big Data Management
CIT453.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the concepts of big data management, focusing on the technologies, tools, and challenges involved in handling large-scale structured and unstructured data sets. Students will gain insights into data storage, processing, analysis, and security within big data environments. Students will understand the principles of big data, analyze and manage large datasets using contemporary big data tools, design and implement scalable big data storage solutions, apply security and privacy measures in big data contexts, and evaluate the performance of big data systems. The course also explores how big data can contribute to sustainability by optimizing resource use, improving environmental monitoring, and supporting green

CIT470.title: Data Mining
CIT470.description: This course introduces the principles of data mining to the students. The students will learn preprocessing of data (data cleaning, data reduction etc.) before applying data mining techniques. Some of the data mining techniques covered in this course are classification, association analysis, and clustering. Students will learn about the social and ethical aspects of data mining. Additionally, the course explores how data mining can support sustainability goals, such as optimizing resource consumption and supporting environmental data analysis. General Track Courses

CIT472.title: User Interface Design
CIT472.description: This course covers user interface design within the software development process, integrating cognitive theories relevant to effective interaction. It includes usability requirements specification and evaluation, emphasizing a multi-disciplinary approach. Students learn to assess user needs and capabilities and how this influence UI development through iterative design phases such as data gathering, analysis, prototyping, construction, and evaluation. The course introduces green computing principles and eco-friendly design practices. Students will use industry-standard tools such as Figma, Adobe XD, Axure RP, and Sketch for wireframing and prototyping; Miro for collaborative brainstorming and user journey mapping; and Usability Hub or Hotjar for usability testing and feedback gathering

CIT473.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
CIT473.description: This course introduces undergraduate students to the fundamental concepts and techniques in Artificial Intelligence (AI). Students will explore how intelligent systems can be designed to solve problems using methods such as search algorithms, rule-based reasoning, and basic machine learning. The course covers key areas including knowledge representation, natural language processing, and AI applications in areas such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and sustainability. Emphasis is placed on how AI technologies can contribute to addressing global challenges such as energy efficiency, climate change, and smart resource management

CIT474.title: Internet of Things
CIT474.description: This course introduces the architecture, protocols, and real- world applications of the Internet of Things (IoT). Students will explore core concepts such as connectivity, interoperability, discoverability, security/privacy, and sustainability in IoT ecosystems. Emphasis is placed on IoT applications in smart cities, industry, and environmental monitoring. The student will be presented to some tools used for building IoT setup, such as TinkerCAD, Arduino simulators, Linux OS, and Python programming environments

CIT477.title: Natural Language Processing
CIT477.description: This course explores the theory and practical aspects of processing human language using computational methods. Topics include text preprocessing, language modeling, part-of- speech tagging, syntactic parsing, semantic analysis, and pragmatic analysis. It also covers applications of NLP techniques such as Named Entity Recognition, Question and Answering Systems, Sentiment Analysis, Topic Modeling, and Sentiment Analysis. Students will gain hands-on experience with NLP tools and libraries. The course also explores how NLP can contribute to sustainability by supporting environmental text analysis and informed decision-making

CIT478.title: Mobile Applications Development
CIT478.description: This course provides comprehensive knowledge related to designing, developing, and deploying mobile applications and websites, aligning with industry practices. It covers design principles, tools, techniques, and methods for mobile application development, including user interface design, data management, security, privacy, and ethics. Students will gain hands-on experience with industry-standard frameworks, testing tools, and deployment methods, preparing them to create secure, scalable, and sustainable mobile applications for diverse industry sectors

CIT481.title: Contemporary Issues in IT
CIT481.description: This course introduces the student to theoretical and technological aspects of a variety of trending IT Topics besides professional, social, ethical, privacy, security and reliability concerns. The technological trends studied are like Cloud Computing, Virtualization, Internet of Things (IoT), Big Data, Machine Learning (ML), Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Blockchain. Emphasis is placed on evaluating the business, environmental, and societal impacts of these technologies and understanding strategies for integrating them successfully within organizational and smart city contexts

CIT483.title: Internship
CIT483.description: This is a supervised course requiring a minimum of 480 hours of structured, industry-based training in Information Technology or related fields. The internship provides students with the opportunity to apply technical skills and academic knowledge to solve real-world IT problems while gaining exposure to current tools, technologies, and practices used in industry, with a focus on sustainability and responsible innovation. Through this experience, students enhance their professional competencies, including teamwork, communication, and time management, and develop an understanding of ethical, social, and environmental considerations in professional IT contexts. Student performance is continuously monitored by an assigned faculty supervisor in collaboration with the workplace supervisor through regular evaluations and progress reviews

CIT484.title: Senior Graduation Project I
CIT484.description: This course provides students with the opportunity to explore a chosen area of interest, conduct in-depth research, and demonstrate independent learning, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Students will apply research methodologies and concepts acquired in earlier coursework to develop a comprehensive project proposal. The process involves selecting a topic, gathering and analyzing relevant information, formulating a clear problem statement, conducting a literature review, and proposing feasible and innovative solutions. Students are expected to apply appropriate methodologies to analyze the problem and develop an initial system design aligned with sustainability principles. Particular emphasis is placed on incorporating environmental, economic, and social dimensions of sustainability into the project’s design and planning. By the end of the course, students will present a preliminary system design and submit a detailed project report that highlights the project’s potential contribution to sustainable development goals (SDGs)

CIT485.title: Senior Graduation Project II
CIT485.description: This supervised course is the continuation of Senior Graduation Project I (CIT484), in which students are expected to fully implement their proposed solution. Building on the design phase and documentation developed in SGP1, students will complete the remaining phases of the project, detailed design, system implementation, testing, validation, and final documentation. Throughout the course, students will apply project management practices, adhere to software engineering methodologies, and receive weekly guidance from their academic supervisor. The course emphasizes sustainable development by encouraging the integration of environmentally and socially responsible practices, such as energy efficiency, ethical data usage, and alignment with national and global Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The course fosters teamwork, independent problem-solving, ethical responsibility, and effective communication, equipping students with practical and professional skills essential for real-world IT project execution. Elective Courses

CIT486.title: Network Protocols
CIT486.description: This applied course introduces students to the concepts, terminology, protocols, and services that the Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP) suite uses to make the Internet work. This course also stimulates hands-on skills development by not only describing TCP/IP capabilities, but also by encouraging students to interact with protocols. It provides troubleshooting knowledge and tools that network administrators and analysts need to keep their systems running smoothly. Moreover, this course will cover topics ranging from characterization to error detection, security analysis and protocols design for sustainable solutions

CIT487.title: Cloud and Edge Computing
CIT487.description: This course covers important concepts, architectures, and service models in an in-depth examination of cloud and edge computing. Theoretical lectures, practical exercises, and case studies give students a thorough understanding of the networking, virtualization, and distributed computing technologies that support these paradigms. Working with top cloud platforms and edge computing frameworks to deploy, maintain, and optimize apps is what practical workshops entail. Additionally, the course explores how cloud and edge computing contribute to sustainability by enabling energy-efficient resource management, reducing data transmission overhead, and supporting green IT initiatives. The course also looks at actual use cases from a variety of industries to show how edge and cloud computing technologies are enabling creative solutions and revolutionizing corporate processes

CIT488.title: Network Virtualization
CIT488.description: This course covers important concepts, architectures, and service models in an in-depth examination of cloud and edge computing. Theoretical lectures, practical exercises, and case studies give students a thorough understanding of the networking, virtualization, and distributed computing technologies that support these paradigms. Working with top cloud platforms and edge computing frameworks to deploy, maintain, and optimize apps is what practical workshops entail. Additionally, the course explores how cloud and edge computing contribute to sustainability by enabling energy-efficient resource management, reducing data transmission overhead, and supporting green IT initiatives. The course also looks at actual use cases from a variety of industries to show how edge and cloud computing technologies are enabling creative solutions and revolutionizing corporate processes

CIT489.title: Advance Network Security
CIT489.description: This course aims to equip the students with the skills needed for analyzing and examining networks’ vulnerabilities and designing secured networks for critical applications. The course focuses on practical experience to meet objectives. Network elements attacks along with protection approaches are addressed: servers, database, operating system, mainframes, and others. Designing secured networks are studied while considering exploiting vulnerabilities with the Nmap scripting engine. Additionally, the course explores sustainable network design practices, such as energy-efficient security solutions and minimizing the environmental impact of network infrastructures. Diploma of Information Technology

DMK305.title: Digital Marketing Fundamentals
