DMK305.description: This course examines the role and impact of digital marketing as a core component of modern business strategies for customer acquisition and retention. Students will gain insights into both the strategic and tactical aspects of digital marketing, exploring essential topics such as the internet value chain, direct-response and database marketing, viral and email marketing, search and mobile marketing, and social media marketing. Key tools and techniques like Google Ads, pay-per-click, affiliate marketing, blogging, storytelling, and digital marketing metrics will be covered. Emphasis is placed on the integration of digital marketing within overall marketing efforts and its alignment with organizational goals, with a focus on emerging technologies and future trends shaping the field

DMK309.title: Sustainability and Responsible Marketing
DMK309.description: This course explores the integration of environmental sustainability, ethical responsibility, and social impact within marketing strategies, with a particular emphasis on digital marketing platforms. The course is designed to equip students with the knowledge and skills to develop marketing strategies that not only achieve business objectives but also foster positive societal and environmental outcomes. The course covers key topics such as consumer behavior and its relation to sustainable consumption, ethical decision-making processes in marketing, green supply chain management, and the design of sustainable products and services. Special focus will be placed on the role of digital marketing tools and technologies, including social media platforms, content marketing, and online campaigns, to amplify messages of sustainability and drive responsible consumer behavior

DMK411.title: Digital Marketing Analytics
DMK411.description: Digital Marketing Analytics focuses on helping managers navigate the complexities of data analysis in the fast-evolving digital world. With rapid advancements in technology and increasing data generation, it's crucial for managers to grasp both the strengths and limitations of popular analytical tools. By doing so, they can uncover patterns and insights in business data to make well-informed decisions. The course provides foundational knowledge in data analysis, along with practical experience with analytical tools, through a mix of lectures, discussions, and interactive sessions. Students will gain hands- on problem-solving skills and learn how to apply various tools in diverse decision-making contexts. Core concepts will be explored through lectures, case discussions, individual exercises, and a team project. As an intensive course, students are expected to complete assigned readings in advance and actively engage in class discussions

DMK415.title: Graduation Project in Digital Marketing
DMK415.description: This course provides an opportunity for students to apply academic tools and analysis techniques to research on a Digital Marketing focused project that aligns with their major and career goals. Offered as a 3-credit course for classroom study or a 6- credit course combining research with an internship, it includes weekly sessions for discussions on idea generation, research methods, and data analysis. Students will also participate in smaller group sessions to present ideas, track progress, and receive feedback. Working individually or in teams, students will complete the course by delivering a case study or research paper on a relevant FinTech topic

DMK419.title: Internship in Digital Marketing
DMK419.description: The course consists of 100 hours of work in a private or public organization. The student may select to have his/her internship in the area of digital marketing. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of LC. Elective Courses

DSAI121.title: Introduction to Computer Architecture for Artificial Intelligence
DSAI121.description: This course introduces the core principles of computer architecture with a focus on AI applications. Students will analyze processor, memory, and I/O architectures, and design digital circuits using Boolean algebra and Karnaugh maps. The course explores GPU, TPU, and ASIC architectures suitable for AI tasks, while highlighting memory organization, parallel cores, and sustainable, power-efficient computing. Special attention is given to sustainability issues related to power dissipation, such as thermal impact, energy consumption trade-offs, and strategies for minimizing environmental footprint through architectural optimization. Emphasizing current hardware trends, students evaluate scalable architectures for AI performance and industrial relevance. Case studies and projects aligned with Industry 4.0 offer hands-on experience with real- world hardware solutions driving innovation in intelligent systems

DSAI212.title: Statistics and Probability for Data Science
DSAI212.description: This course introduces fundamental concepts in probability and statistics, including events and sample spaces, conditional probability, and random variables. Students will explore probability distributions, cumulative and probability density functions, and moments of random variables. The course also covers key statistical topics such as descriptive statistics, sampling methods, sampling distributions, statistical inference, t-tests, analysis of variance (ANOVA) with one and two factors, randomized complete block design, correlation, regression analysis, and chi-square tests. Emphasis is placed on practical applications and model development relevant to data science

DSAI215.title: Introduction to Data Science
DSAI215.description: This course introduces students to foundational data science concepts and their engineering applications. Students will learn data acquisition, preprocessing, and visualization techniques. Through hands-on programming and experimentation, they will develop basic data workflows, assess data quality, and communicate findings using appropriate standards and tools. The course emphasizes engineering practices, reproducibility, and ethical considerations in data-driven problem solving. In addition, sustainability issues such as the environmental impact of large-scale data storage and computation, energy-efficient algorithm design, and responsible data engineering practices are explored, highlighting the role of data science in promoting sustainable development

DSAI310.title: Data Structures & Algorithms Design
DSAI310.description: This course introduces fundamental data structures and algorithms, focusing on their implementation, efficiency, and complexity analysis using Big O notation. Students develop the ability to apply and compare core structures such as arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, and graphs, and algorithms like recursion, searching, and sorting to solve computational sustainable problems effectively

DSAI312.title: Data Analytics
DSAI312.description: Data Analytics is an advanced course designed for students who have completed foundational studies in Data Science. It focuses on developing the ability to conduct comprehensive analyses across various data types and real-world contexts. Students will be engaged in the full spectrum of data analytics, including descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analyses, to derive insights, forecast outcomes, and support data-driven decision- making. The course emphasizes practical skills in data preparation, model selection, and result interpretation, with applications spanning business, technology, scientific and sustainability domains. Through hands-on projects and critical evaluation of analytical techniques, students will learn to align methods with the specific structure and goals of each dataset, preparing them to address complex analytical challenges with confidence and precision

DSAI313.title: Data Analytics Lab
DSAI313.description: This course introduces core concepts in data analytics through practical lab sessions using industry-standard tools. Students will engage in data wrangling, visualization, predictive modeling, and big data analytics, while applying solutions to real-world business and sustainability challenges. The course provides hands-on experience with tools such as Python (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn) for data processing and machine learning, R (ggplot2, plotly) for visualization, Tableau and Power BI for business intelligence dashboards, and Hadoop and Apache Spark for big data processing. By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze datasets effectively and communicate insights through professional data-driven reports and dashboards

DSAI314.title: Advanced Data Science
DSAI314.description: This course deepens students’ understanding of data science by exploring advanced modeling techniques including machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing. Students design and implement complex data pipelines, evaluate models using ethical frameworks, and apply feature engineering and big data tools. The course emphasizes critical thinking, project execution, and deployment of scalable solutions aligned with real-world engineering challenges preparing the needed insights for strategic decision making

DSAI316.title: Data Engineering
DSAI316.description: This course introduces students to the fundamentals of modern data ecosystems. It covers essential data engineering tasks such as managing, extracting, transforming, and loading (ETL) data. Students will explore various data modeling techniques applicable to structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data types. The course also details the data lifecycle within data analytics projects, including data collection (e.g., importing and crawling), preprocessing (cleaning and transformation), ingestion, and warehousing. Additionally, foundational data visualization techniques are introduced to support data understanding and exploration. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to perform key data engineering processes essential for analytics projects. The course emphasizes how data engineering can contribute to sustainability by optimizing energy-efficient workflows, minimizing data redundancy, and supporting data-driven solutions for sustainable development challenges

DSAI317.title: AI Ethics and Policy
DSAI317.description: This course explores the ethical, social, and policy implications of Artificial Intelligence (AI). It examines foundational concepts in AI and data science ethics, key ethical principles, frameworks, and policies that guide the responsible development, deployment, and use of AI and data science technologies. The course encourages critical thinking on AI’s impact on society, privacy, accountability, sustainability, and human rights

DSAI318.title: Internship
DSAI318.description: This internship course is designed to provide students with practical, industry-based experience in the field of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. Students will work with host organizations to apply theoretical knowledge, develop professional skills, and engage in real-world problem-solving. The internship emphasizes hands-on experience, industry exposure, and alignment with engineering principles, including sustainability and ethical responsibilities

DSAI320.title: AI and Sustainable Development
DSAI320.description: This course explores the intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and sustainable development, emphasizing how AI and data science can address global challenges such as climate change, resource management, and social equity. Students will learn to apply AI techniques, such as machine learning, data analytics, and decision support systems to develop innovative, data-driven solutions that promote environmental, economic, and social sustainability. The course integrates foundational concepts of sustainability with practical AI applications, highlighting ethical considerations, responsible innovation, and the societal impact of AI technologies

DSAI321.title: Reinforcement Learning
DSAI321.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to both foundational concepts and cutting-edge techniques in reinforcement learning (RL), a pivotal area of artificial intelligence focused on training agents to make sequential decisions through interactions with dynamic and uncertain environments. Students will delve into core RL frameworks such as Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), value-based methods, policy optimization, Q-learning, and deep reinforcement learning. The course emphasizes rigorous mathematical modeling, practical algorithm implementation, and critical evaluation of RL approaches. Real-world applications including robotics, recommendation systems, game AI, and autonomous systems, serve as illustrative case studies. Additionally, the course fosters engineering problem-solving skills and addresses important ethical and sustainability considerations surrounding autonomous decision-making and AI deployment

DSAI412.title: Data Visualization
DSAI412.description: This course provides students with foundational knowledge and skills in data visualization, focusing on the effective communication of quantitative and qualitative information. The course explores key concepts such as data types, visual perception, design principles, and encoding strategies to transform raw data into meaningful visual representations. Students will utilize industry-relevant tools such as Tableau, Power BI, Python (Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly), and Dataiku to develop visualizations that support engineering analysis, decision-making, and problem-solving. Emphasis is placed on critically evaluating visualizations, designing clear and ethical data displays, and presenting data-driven findings to technical and non-technical audiences

DSAI413.title: Pattern Recognition
DSAI413.description: This course introduces the fundamentals of pattern recognition, emphasizing statistical and structural techniques for the classification and analysis of data patterns. Students will learn to design, implement, and evaluate recognition systems using modern tools, with applications such as handwriting recognition, image classification, and speech processing. The course also encourages the exploration of sustainability-focused applications of pattern recognition, such as environmental data analysis, energy consumption forecasting, and smart resource management systems. Emphasis is placed on developing analytical skills, model selection, and implementation strategies essential for building intelligent and sustainable pattern recognition systems

DSAI416.title: Data Science Applications
DSAI416.description: This course focuses on the implementation of data science solutions across diverse engineering domains such as healthcare, smart cities, and business. Students will analyze domain-specific problems, design and develop data-driven applications, and integrate multiple data sources and APIs. Emphasis is placed on evaluating performance, ensuring sustainability, interpretability, and addressing legal, ethical, and societal impacts of deployed models

DSAI420.title: Business Intelligence
DSAI420.description: This course explores the principles and practices of Business Intelligence (BI), including data warehousing, ETL processes, dashboard design, and performance measurement. Students will utilize industry-standard BI tools to analyze business data, build visualizations, and communicate insights effectively. The course integrates ethical analysis, sustainability issues, real-time analytics, and project-based learning aligned with engineering and organizational decision-making needs

DSAI424.title: Robotic Process Automation
DSAI424.description: This course provides students with the knowledge and skills to design, develop, and deploy software bots for automating rule- based business processes. Students will identify automation opportunities, work with RPA platforms, and implement robust workflows with appropriate error handling and governance. The course highlights best practices, sustainability issues, ethical considerations, and documentation standards essential for scalable automation in engineering contexts

DSAI455.title: Introduction to Software Engineering
DSAI455.description: This course offers a broad overview of software engineering principles, focusing on software products, development processes, and software lifecycle. Students will gain practical experience in Object-Oriented Analysis and Design using the Unified Process (UP) and Unified Modeling Language (UML), including use case, analysis, and class diagram modeling. The course also covers modern topics such as Agile methodologies, DevOps (DevSecOps, SecDevOps, DevOpsSec), and key issues in software security and privacy taking into consideration sustainability and international standards meeting designs. Elective Courses

DSAI482.title: Selected Topics in Data Science
DSAI482.description: This course offers students the opportunity to explore specialized or emerging areas of Data Science beyond the standard curriculum. Each semester, a distinct topic—such as Big Data Engineering, Deep Learning for Natural Language Processing, Ethical AI and Responsible Data Use, Cloud-based Data Analytics, Real-Time Streaming Analytics, Data Visualization for Decision Support, or Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning—is selected and approved. Through lectures, labs, case studies, and projects, students gain in-depth exposure to advanced concepts, methods, and tools used in contemporary data science practice and research. The course emphasizes hands-on experience, critical thinking, and ethical and sustainability considerations when applying data science in real- world contexts. Bachelor of Information Technology (BIT)—General Track Core Courses

DSAI490.title: Senior Design Project 1
DSAI490.description: This course represents the initial phase of the Senior Design Project, where students work in teams to identify a relevant problem in the field of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, ensuring alignment with sustainability goals and industry standards. Students are expected to apply theoretical knowledge and practical skills acquired from prior coursework to analyze the problem, design a feasible solution model, test the developed model, verify that it meets the required standards, and develop essential project documentation. These include a detailed project proposal, budget, timeline, and task plan. Emphasis is placed on collaborative teamwork, professional communication, and the integration of ethical and societal considerations. At the end of the course, students will demonstrate their ability to plan and initiate a data-driven engineering project with clear objectives, resource planning, and stakeholder-focused communication

DSAI491.title: Senior Design Project 2
DSAI491.description: This course is the second phase of the Senior Design Project 1, where students continue the development and completion of their research project related to Data Science and Artificial Intelligence. Building on the foundation of Senior Graduation Project I, students will focus on project implementation, verification, validation, development, evaluation, and final documentation. This course emphasizes technical proficiency, problem-solving, and effective communication of project outcomes, with a strong focus on sustainability principles and alignment with industry standards

ECB305.title: E-Commerce Fundamental
ECB305.description: This course introduces fundamental concepts in e-commerce, covering various e-commerce models, technologies, strategies, and their applications in the digital marketplace. Emphasis will be on understanding the infrastructure, security, payment systems, and regulatory frameworks that support e-commerce. The course explores case studies from the region, focusing on how businesses utilize e-commerce for growth and sustainability

ECB401.title: E-Supply Chain Management
ECB401.description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of supply chain management (SCM) in the digital age, focusing on the integration of electronic systems, data analytics, and global logistics. This course will focus on supply chain strategy, logistics information systems, segmental positioning, order management and fulfillment, inventory, forecasting and collaborative planning. Student attention is directed to digital logistics as a value-adding process that achieves time and place synchronization of demand with operational fulfillment

ECB413.title: Business Driven Technology
ECB413.description: The course emphasizes the critical role of technology in driving business initiatives, focusing on a business-first approach to technology solutions. It provides students with a comprehensive understanding of how organizations leverage technology to achieve strategic goals, improve operations, and drive innovation within the e-commerce sector. Key areas of study include IT infrastructure, data management, business intelligence, customer relationship management (CRM) systems, cybersecurity, and the integration of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, and cloud computing

ECB415.title: Graduation Project in E-Commerce
ECB415.description: This course provides an opportunity for students to apply academic tools and analysis techniques to research on an E- Commerce focused project that aligns with their major and career goals. Offered as a 3-credit course for classroom study or a 6-credit course combining research with an internship, it includes weekly sessions for discussions on idea generation, research methods, and data analysis. Students will also participate in smaller group sessions to present ideas, track progress, and receive feedback. Working individually or in teams, students will complete the course by delivering a case study or research paper on a relevant to the field of E-commerce

ECB419.title: Internship in E-Commerce
ECB419.description: The course consists of 100 hours of work in a private or public organization. The student may select to have his/her internship in the area of E-Commerce or information technology. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of LU Elective Courses

ECM210.title: Introduction To Paramedicine
ECM210.description: This course introduces the student to the psychological and physical demands of emergency medical provider. It introduces information in preparation for the student’s progress throughout the entire paramedic program. Beginning with a basic introduction to the profession and roles and responsibilities, the foundation of knowledge for the emergency medical care systems. Legal and ethical issues related to the patients and duty of EMS, workforce safety and wellness will be covered

ECM211.title: Patient Assessment
ECM211.description: This course introduces student to the patient assessment undertaken by paramedic. The course provides necessary knowledge and skills for patient assessment and re-assessment including scene size-up, primary and secondary assessment as overview for a trauma and medical patient

ECM220.title: Airway & Respiratory Emergencies
ECM220.description: This course is designed to provide the students with the essential knowledge to evaluate and deal with airway and respiratory emergency medical cases including pathophysiological interpretation and assessment. These are emergencies of the upper and lower airway that compromise the respiratory system

ECM221.title: Trauma I
ECM221.description: This course introduces the Paramedic Student to Trauma and Trauma Systems. It prepares students to Perform Comprehensive Patient Assessment with various Injury Patterns, recognizing various mechanisms of injuries like Blunt Trauma, Penetrating Trauma, and managing Bleeding with External and Internal Haemorrhage, Soft Tissue injuries & Burns, orthopedic injuries and Environmental Injuries

ECM310.title: Trauma II
ECM310.description: This course is designed to provide more focus on practical trauma instruction. It covers: blunt trauma, penetrating trasuma, haemorrhage and shock, soft tissue trauma, burn conditions, musculoskeletal trauma and gaining access and extrication. It also covers the initial aspect of students traumatic skills related to the above topics

ECM311.title: Cardiovascular I
ECM311.description: This course focuses on the cardiovascular anatomy and physiology, conducting system of the heart, electrocardiography, as well as interpretation and the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias, interpretation of 3 and 12 lead EKGs (including injury and ischemia patterns, normal and abnormal findings, and the 12 lead as a diagnostic tool) will be covered. Principles of ACS diagnosis/management will be laboratory focus of this course

ECM312.title: Medical Emergencies
ECM312.description: This course covers medical evaluation and treatment of medical emergencies including pathophysiological interpretation and assessment of pulmonary, neurology, endocrinology, gastroenterology, urology and nephrology, toxicology and substance abuse, Haematology and behavioral disorders. It covers the initial aspect of patient assessment and medical skills related to all above topics

ECM313.title: Paramedic Clinical Practice I
ECM313.description: This course focuses on the cardiovascular anatomy and physiology, conducting system of the heart, electrocardiography, as well as interpretation and the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias, interpretation of 3 and 12 lead EKGs (including injury and ischemia patterns, normal and abnormal findings, and the 12 lead as a diagnostic tool) will be covered. Principles of ACS diagnosis/management will be laboratory focus of this course

ECM320.title: Obstetrics and Pediatric Emergencies
ECM320.description: This course covers medical evaluation and treatment of gynecological, obstetrics, and pediatric patients. Initial patient assessment and medical skills related to all above topics

ECM321.title: EMC Operations I
ECM321.description: This course prepares the paramedic student to take part in the management of emergency incidents in pre-hospital environment such as vehicle accidents, other major incidents related to injury triangle (driver, road, vehicle) It covers materials related to ambulance operations, medical incident management, vehicle extrication and special rescue awareness & operations, hazardous materials incidents, disasters, crime scene awareness, rural ems, and responding to terrorist acts. Major topics covered

ECM410.title: Special Patient Populations
ECM410.description: This course covers advanced patient assessment techniques in special patient populations. Topics include initial assessment, medical trauma history, field impression, complete physical exam process, on-going assessment and documentation skills. It also includes scenarios and problem-based assessment management

ECM411.title: Cardiovascular II
ECM411.description: This course focuses on advanced cardiology, identification of life threatening and non-life-threatening cardiac emergencies. It includes how to analyze standard 3-lead (revision) and 12- lead Electrocardiogram (EKG) information and determine a plan of action. Management of cardiopulmonary arrest and other cardiovascular emergencies using the American Heart Association standards will be covered

ECM420.title: EMC Operations II
ECM420.description: This course prepares the paramedic student to theoretical and practical foundations that are necessary for pre-planning and management of mass gathering events with a special focus on, sports and other mass gathering events. This will also cover management of incidents involving multiple casualties with multiple agencies like police, fire, hazmat, and NDRF. Topics include foundations of disaster planning, incident command system, weapons of mass destruction, response issues, and hazardous materials incidents

ECM421.title: Trauma III
ECM421.description: This course introduces the paramedic student to advanced level of trauma and trauma systems to perform comprehensive patient assessment with various injury patterns, recognizing and managing chest injuries, abdominal, genitourinary, and environmental trauma and managing and resuscitating patient with critical care injuries

ECM422.title: Paramedic Clinical Practice II
ECM422.description: This course prepares the student for paramedic clinical practice that consist of specific number of distributed rotations inside the hospital settings in ERS, ICU, SICU, RICU, PICU, NICU, CCU to perform hands on skills at a basic level such as patient assessment, physical examination, vital signs, and others in the triage section, and performing advanced skills like intravenous insertion, medication administration and advance management of cardiopulmonary emergencies and special consideration situations including paediatrics’ and geriatrics, and procedures taught thus far in the program

ECM510.title: Graduation Project
ECM510.description: This course provides students with the opportunity to apply research skills and carry out a research project related to the major program under the supervision of a faculty member. Students will be required to conduct literature review and perform data collection, statistical analysis, writing up of the research paper. Students participating in research must complete CITI program (https://about.citiprogram.org/en/homepage/) for research ethics and compliance training prior to submitting research proposals

ECM511.title: Specialized Emergency Care
ECM511.description: This course introduces the student to the concepts of involvement in specialized scenarios and situations such as military field medicine including environmental emergencies, aviation medicine, and diving medicine. This course will cover paediatric advanced life support (PALS). It also covers the initial aspect of patient assessment and medical skills related to all above topics

ECM512.title: Paramedic Clinical Practice III
ECM512.description: This course prepares students for paramedic clinical practice that consist of ambulance rotations out of hospital settings in pre- hospital care settings to perform hands on skills at a basic level such as patient lifting and moving, patient assessment, physical examination, vital signs, and performing advanced skills like intravenous insertion, medication administration and advance management of cardiopulmonary emergencies and special considerations situation including paediatrics’ and geriatrics, procedures taught thus far in the program

ECM520.title: Paramedic Clinical Practice IV
ECM520.description: This course prepares student to advanced paramedic clinical practice that consist clinical/field rotation of 16 weeks period. It is an essential component of the EMCM program, which will serve as a summative or ‘capstone’ evaluation of their achievement of the objectives and goals of the program. This paramedic clinical/field internship rotations are intended to offer internship paramedics both a positive learning opportunity and real-life experiences, in assessing, treating and managing real patients while being guided by experienced and competent emergency health care professionals. The purpose of this rotation is to allow advanced paramedic to act as the ‘in charge’ medic. They are expected to be able to ‘run’ the call at the same level of competence as an entry-level paramedic. In addition to the appropriate interaction, assessment and management of all patients, the student should focus on the overall integration of everything they have learned as well as ‘scene management’. During this advanced clinical practice rotation, paramedic students should participate in all basic and advanced EMS procedures related to patient assessment and management, ACLS interventions, use of mechanical ventilators, perform neuro-vitals and use advanced monitoring devices. Students must be exposed to patients of different ages and with various pathologies. Ideally, they should be responding and receiving satisfactory ratings Bachelor of Science in Respiratory Care Core Major Courses

ENG100.title: English 1
ENG100.prerequisites: One of the English proficiency Tests (Emst, IELTS,TOEFL etc.)
ENG100.description: The course is designed for college students to benefit from an intensive skill-building curriculum that targets the main English skills. The focus of the course will be on reading and writing skill practice, grammar and structure application, and integration across the disciplines at the college-level. Students will be expected to successfully demonstrate and apply appropriate college-level reading and writing skills to a variety of assignments and assessments. Competences in contextualized reading and writing skills will be developed. Active reading and writing strategies will be learned through practice and application. COLLEGE OF BUSINESS Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting Core Courses for Business Programs

ENG104.title: English 2
ENG104.description: This is a writing course that helps students become competent writers by engaging them in the writing process and by encouraging them to explore and organize their ideas in writing well-organized and developed paragraphs and essays. Students also study grammar, basic sentence structure and mechanics. Written and communication Skills will be developed and improved to prepare students for future careers

FIN301.title: Introduction to Fintech and Big Data
FIN301.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of big data in finance and FinTech, covering data sources, analytics techniques, and applications in financial modeling, risk management, customer insights, and fraud detection. Emphasizing data quality, governance, and security, the course examines blockchain's role in enhancing transparency and addresses privacy concerns. Future trends, including AI and machine learning, are also explored to prepare students for evolving challenges and opportunities in the FinTech landscape

FIN302.title: Introduction to Blockchain and Digital Currencies
FIN302.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of digital transformation in global finance, focusing on Industry 4.0, blockchain, and artificial intelligence. Students will examine cryptocurrency trading, mining, and exchange dynamics, as well as blockchain's role in securing digital transactions and enabling business automation. Key topics include regulatory and ethical considerations, entrepreneurial opportunities in digital finance, and strategies for navigating the evolving digital finance landscape. The course concludes with insights into global blockchain adaptation and career guidance in blockchain, cryptocurrency, and FinTech

FIN303.title: Innovation, Entrepreneurial Finance, and Fintech
FIN303.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of entrepreneurial finance in emerging markets, focusing on the diverse funding needs of startups and the options available to them. Topics include venture capital, bootstrapping, angel investing, bank financing, and alternative sources such as government programs and incubators. Students will also examine FinTech innovations, challenges for women entrepreneurs, and the impact of policy on access to finance. The course concludes with a comparative analysis of financing options and future research directions, preparing students to navigate and support the growth of entrepreneurial ventures

FIN415.title: Graduation Project in FinTech
FIN415.description: This course provides an opportunity for students to apply academic tools and analysis techniques to research a FinTech- focused project that aligns with their major and career goals. Offered as a 3-credit course for classroom study or a 6-credit course combining research with an internship, it includes weekly sessions for discussions on idea generation, research methods, and data analysis. Students will also participate in smaller group sessions to present ideas, track progress, and receive feedback. Working individually or in teams, students will complete the course by delivering a case study or research paper on a relevant FinTech topic

FIN419.title: Internship in FinTech
FIN419.description: The course consists of 100 hours of work in a private or public organization. The student may select to have his/her internship in any area of business administration or information technology. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of LC

GEN103.title: Critical Thinking
GEN103.description: Critical Thinking is a course designed to help students develop their skills in reasoning, analysis, and the use of logical arguments. This course introduces students to the standards of critical thinking, nature of arguments, deductive and inductive reasoning, fallacious reasoning, role of language, critical analysis, and evaluation. The students are also introduced to the basic skills of good reasoning needed for the intelligent and responsible conduct of life. The course also includes the application of concepts in familiar areas and current issues, to help students develop practical and useful logical and critical thinking skills to understand and appreciate viewpoints which are different from their own

GEN201.title: Psychology
GEN201.description: This course is capstone course that attempts to addresses the major theories, principles, and methodologies of psychology with special emphasis on their relations to human behavior. The biological foundations of behavior, sensory processes, learning, perception, memory, emotion, motivation, personality, and the social basis of behavior are examined

GEN302.title: Fundamentals of Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
GEN302.description: This course seeks to prepare students how to apply core concepts regarding design thinking process, innovation, entrepreneurship and sustainability to organizations in the UAE. Students will learn how to connect entrepreneurship to the UAE community and economy and how as entrepreneurs can utilize design thinking and innovation to establish their start-up enterprises Design thinking, Entrepreneurship, and Growth and Leadership are three modules that will be covered throughout course delivery, study questions, videos, and projects

GEN304.title: Ethics
GEN304.description: This course exposes students to core concepts, ideals and practical issues regarding professional ethics and moral behaviors. The history and development, ethical guidelines/principles and contemporary theories of the subject- matter will be the focus of the introductory chapter. Furthermore, discussions will concentrate on the relevance of Professional Ethics to modern workplaces and environments. Morality and liability, employees and moral choices, employers, and moral choices, are themes which will be covered throughout course delivery, exams and case studies

HCM120.title: Principles of Health Management
HCM120.description: This course is designed to introduce students to key concepts related to the principle of health management, including concepts, issues, organizations, policies, strategies of health management approaches. The provided knowledge will deal with discipline matters of management principles applied to health services offering students an exploration of an overview of health management, strategic management, decision-making, assessment of information need, human resource management, leadership, team building, health management conflict, time management, operational health planning, program monitoring and evaluation

HCM211.title: Healthcare Services Management
HCM211.description: The market for health services is global and growing. Demographic changes and advances in health service knowledge are driving a need for health service managers who can organize large and complex operations and coordinate diverse professions exist in healthcare entities. Demand for health services continues to be strong internationally across public, private, and not-for-profit sectors. This course is designed to support students who wish to move into managerial positions within the health services industry; complementing previous professional/academic qualifications or building upon workplace experience. It combines insights to both public and private healthcare services with contemporary management theory. This course is designed to develop students' skills in both strategic and operational issues pertaining to healthcare services. Students will study the importance of blending technology, people, marketing, and information to achieve a distinctive competitive outcomes and high standards of healthcare quality. Concepts taught include service management, service quality, customer satisfaction, and developing service/qualify solutions for healthcare providers

HCM212.title: Healthcare Delivery System
HCM212.description: This course is designed to optimize students' views regards the health care system and how it is delivered. It demonstrates an overview of the health care delivery system and how performance assessing and how process improvements could be managed. It provides an overview of the health care systems and its components in the United Arab Emirates with emphasis on the types of providers and the role that accrediting, and licensing bodies play in the delivery of health care. The course focuses on the unique characteristics of health care delivery and discusses the major issues and challenges that impact the cost, quality, and access to health care. Emphasis is placed on understanding the historical context; how the UAE health care system developed; and the significant policies that regulate health care organizations, providers, payers, and populations. Students are introduced also to general technology, financial, reimbursement, legal, and strategic planning issues that are essential to managing in the health care environment

HCM224.title: Legal Aspects and Ethics in Health Management
HCM224.description: This course is designed to provide students with an introduction to health law and ethics. It starts with ethical theories, principles, and tools that are important when making ethical decisions. Then explores privacy and confidentiality within the context of the many uses of health information, and covers ethical dilemmas faced in the process of protected health information, clinical coding, pricing, access, and quality management. It addresses the importance of patient safety and organizational values, research, and decision support for data acquisition, access, and reporting. The course will include a discussion of the UAE system of laws and regulations of healthcare providers; legal and ethical issues in providing health care services to patients; legal and ethical issues in organizing, managing, and regulating the delivery of health care services; and legal issues in health insurance programs

HCM225.title: Hospital Administration
HCM225.description: As rapid Scientific, technological, and medical advances in recent years have completely transformed the health care sector. Hospitals have become a dynamic industry. Professionals who are responsible for planning and designing hospitals and those who subsequently manage, maintain, and operate them efficiently find the task of managing change quite challenging. This course is a broad subject that will let students understand the basics as well as the complexities of managing a hospital well. It has lots of ideas for the architect, who conceives of a viable plan for the hospital. It addresses the various issues which must be kept in mind by consultants, planners, and administrators who subsequently run the hospital. This course will cover most, Planning and Designing a hospital: The Correct Way, Planning and Designing Medical and Ancillary Services, Planning and Designing Nursing Services, Supportive Services, Facilities Planning for Managing SARS, CATH Lab, Hospital Information System, and Telemedicine

HCM307.title: Introduction to Health promotion and Disease Prevention
HCM307.description: This course is designed to introduce the basics principle of disease management responsible for efficient and systematic control of the creation. The course will orientate the students to critical concepts of self-management and health promotion, and explore the nature of the multidisciplinary team, maintenance, use and disposition of records, including processes for capturing and maintaining evidence and information about how to prepares students for the practice in the field of symptom management of people with chronic disease and/or life-limiting illness (LLI) and palliative care, and lays the foundation for further study in this field. The course as well will focus on the health promotion and models of health promotion, and principles of health behavior change, to encourage the individual to adopt healthy behaviors

HCM312.title: Medical Insurance Systems
HCM312.description: This course introduces students to the problem of risk, and health insurance, medical health insurance, and disability income insurance, and other topics such as social insurance programs, the private insurance industry, and regulation of insurance industry. Additionally, it explores methods such as health insurance claim processing and treatment approval. The course uses the understanding of the general principles of health insurance as a tool to understand the cooperative health insurance program implemented in the UAE

HCM320.title: Management Processes in Health Service Organizations
HCM320.description: This course is providing students with the tools to significantly improve health care organizational operations and processes as well as enhance quality and customer satisfaction by ensuring that services are tightly synchronized with patterns of patient demand. This course will cover the application of the concepts and methods of operation management to the health care organizational setting with an emphasis on planning and control in the management process. Students are taught to identify common bottlenecks and constraints and focus on the critical issues and processes faced by managers in the health care field

HCM322.title: Healthcare Economics
HCM322.description: This course builds on students’ previous course and work experiences and introduces students to the concepts and tools needed to provide an opportunity for deepening their understanding of various business and social science theories, principles and models and how they do, or do not, apply within the healthcare sector. The course explores the development and delivery of services, tangible goods and ideas (social marketing) in the health sector by for-profit and non-profit organizations in developed and developing countries. To put knowledge to practice, student teams undertake consulting projects in local healthcare institutions and organizations. The course covered the case studies, readings, lectures, discussions, and web-based sources, therefore, the students become aware of the complexity of decision making in health care, and the development of the value proposition

HCM323.title: Quality Management in Healthcare
HCM323.description: This course stresses the importance of continuous improvement of healthcare to avoid medical errors with their associated dilemmas. Introduces the principles of healthcare quality management and its significant role in applying evidence-based healthcare practices. It provides the students with essential tool and skills to monitoring, managing, measuring and improving the performance of healthcare organizations and professionals. Meeting patient’s needs and expectations and adopting effective functions and processes that increase the probability of achieving the desired healthcare outcomes, and create Patient Safety Culture in healthcare entities. It stresses the importance of “Lean Healthcare” and the Total Quality Management” to manage healthcare variations and ensure high standard of healthcare quality and many other approces derived from them such as “error proofing, Six Sigma, Visual Management, Standardization, 5S, and Kanban

HCM325.title: First Aid and Safety
HCM325.description: As rapid Scientific, technological, and medical advances in recent years have completely transformed the health care sector. Hospitals have become a dynamic industry. Professionals who are responsible for planning and designing hospitals and those who subsequently manage, maintain, and operate them efficiently find the task of managing change quite challenging. This course is a broad subject that will let students understand the basics as well as the complexities of managing a hospital well. It has lots of ideas for the architect, who conceives of a viable plan for the hospital. It addresses the various issues which must be kept in mind by consultants, planners, and administrators who subsequently run the hospital. This course will cover most, Planning and Designing a hospital: The Correct Way, Planning and Designing Medical and Ancillary Services, Planning and Designing Nursing Services, Supportive Services, Facilities Planning for Managing SARS, CATH Lab, Hospital Information System, and Telemedicine

HCM412.title: Health Policy
HCM412.description: This course provides a framework for developing and analyzing a range of health policy issues. The course begins by introducing an approach for rationally analyzing any public health policy issues. The course also has relevant topics on; other models of the policy process and analyzing historical, political, ethical, and legal ramifications, assessing the need and demand, examining economic and financial considerations, assessing existing programs and policies

HCM413.title: Strategic Healthcare Planning
HCM413.description: This course provides the basis for understanding what leadership is and what leaders do to be successful. This course will look at how successful leaders develop a vision for the future, align other behind their vision, and motivate them to achieve the vision. This course will review theories of leadership and analyze common strategies used by leaders, both effective and ineffective, as well as address moral and ethical responsibility of leadership

HCM414.title: Information Governance for Health Professionals
HCM414.description: This course introduces students to the global transformation of information in health to electronic formats, health organizations need to invest in improved information governance systems to ensure health data is private and secure. The course will discuss the information governance regulations and policies to support the creation, storage, use, retention, and destruction of healthcare data. The course will cover the principles of information governance, how information governance can support and maintain the information life-cycle, the impact of technology transformation, privacy and security of healthcare data, healthcare policy and other regulatory considerations, risk management and strategy, and building a culture of information governance. Bach elor of Science in Emergency Medical Care Core Major Courses

HIM210.title: Introduction to Healthcare Informatics
HIM210.description: This course is an introduction to the health information management profession and the heath record focusing on procedures for completion, maintenance, and preservation of health information in the UAE. The relationship between health information management and the health care delivery system in the UAE and other countries will be discussed. Topics covered include the content and structure of patient records; quantitative and qualitative analyses of the documentation of patient care; storage methods; and retrieving patient data. There will also be a discussion of clinical classification types employed in Health Information Management

HIM320.title: Medical Coding I
HIM320.description: This course introduces students to the International Classification of Disease (ICD-10-CM) coding system. Topics covered include the guidelines and terminology for correctly coding diagnoses in a physician’s office, hospital, or other healthcare facility as well as the assigning and sequencing of diagnostic and procedural codes. Emphasis will be on the recent change from ICD-9-CM to ICD-10-CM and the implications of this change

HIM321.title: Health Data Concepts
HIM321.description: This course introduces students to the International Classification of Disease (ICD-10-CM) coding system. Topics covered include the guidelines and terminology for correctly coding diagnoses in a physician’s office, hospital, or other healthcare facility as well as the assigning and sequencing of diagnostic and procedural codes. Emphasis will be on the recent change from ICD-9-CM to ICD-10-CM and the implications of this change

HIM410.title: Medical Coding II
HIM410.description: This course is a continuation of Coding I and provides students with an introduction to the nomenclature of Current Procedure Terminology (CPT®). Topics include detailed application of the CPT classification system for inpatient services such as surgery and anesthesia as well as for outpatient such as laboratory and radiology. There will also be a discussion of evaluation and management services, as well as the use of modifiers

HIM411.title: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Management Transformation
HIM411.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of how Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming healthcare management. Drawing from best practices in digital transformation and AI strategy, students will examine AI implementation frameworks, emerging technologies, change management, and ethical considerations. Emphasis is placed on strategic integration, operational efficiency, and innovation to prepare future healthcare leaders to oversee and direct digital transformation initiatives

HRM201.title: Introduction to Human resource Management
HRM201.description: This course introduces various areas of human resource management including its strategic role, job analysis, training and development, HR planning and recruitment, employee selection, training and developing employees, performance management, strategic pay plans, employee relations, and employee safety & health in the workplace

HRM301.title: Recruitment and Selection
HRM301.description: This is a core course discussing various areas of HR Planning and Recruitment including job analysis and recruitment, recruitment in labor markets, legal and ethical considerations in recruitment, managing diversity & equal employment, selecting and placing human resources, interviewing, employee testing, retention of employees, compensation and employee performance. Attention is given to some specific topics from these areas so more crucial concepts/methods may be dealt with in-depth

HRM303.title: Training and Development
HRM303.description: This course introduces the design, delivery and assessment of training programs in businesses and other organizations. Practical importance is placed on the development of training programs and evaluation instruments, as well as on the use of effective instructional methods to deliver these programs with emphasis on applying learning theories to the training function. Bachelor of Business Administratio n in Business Information Technology Major Courses

HRM401.title: Compensation
HRM401.description: This is a major course introducing the students with various areas of compensation and benefit practices including compensation strategies, job-based structure, job evaluation, building and maintaining compensation structure, incentive plans, pay for performance, employee benefits and legal issues in compensation. Attention is given to some specific topics from these areas so more in-depth understanding of crucial concepts/methods is attained

HRM403.title: Occupational health and safety
HRM403.description: This course will develop knowledge in the area of occupational health and safety management and will give students a critical introduction to the broad subject of OHS to examine in detail some of the specific theoretical and practical issues related to the topic. Moreover, this course will integrate topical workplace health and safety issues into the context of previous studies to provide students with skills to analyze, evaluate current trends in OHS

HRM407.title: Performance Management
HRM407.description: This course is discussing the major theories and practices related to Performance Management. It examines HR performance assessment and types of evaluation and appraisal systems, the relation between the performance appraisal and the succession, training, incentive systems, planning, empowerment, and HR development. It also deals with the most common performance problems faced by HR officers, explaining the techniques they can use to improve the workforce performance and stability in their vocations and in the organization

HRM409.title: Labor Relations
HRM409.description: This course introduces the student with the main issues of labor relations and integrates learning material with examples from the UAE and GCC. It covers areas including labor relations; Emirates labor laws, labor unions, bargaining issues, process of negotiations, contract administration, and organizational conflict. This course surveys the effects of employment dynamics, Union organization and representation, collective bargaining and negotiation, grievance and arbitration processes, labor laws and governmental agencies regulating labor practice Contemporary issues on labor-management relations in the public and private sectors of the workplace

HRM410.title: Strategic Human Resource Management
HRM410.description: Making the balance between theoretical approaches in SHRM and their reflection in the key practical issues that the HR managers face, this course provides the students with the necessary knowledge about the strategic dimension of HRM and the necessary skills for its implementation to the different HRM practices and policies

HRM412.title: Labor Laws
HRM412.description: This course is a critical component of the BBA in Human Resource Management. It completes students’ knowledge of HRM practices by adding the essential knowledge of UAE labor law as a frame of reference for analyzing, conducting, and monitoring HR practices in UAE’s public as well as private organizations. The course focuses on legislation related to employment conditions, such as hiring, working hours, vacation, type of employment contracts (Unlimited and Limited) and termination of employment. This course discusses the principle of labor laws and regulations affecting the legal relationship between organizations and their employees. Topics include basic concepts such as: fair employment practices, Equal Employment Opportunities (EEO), affirmative action, and employee rights and protections. Upon completion, students should be able to evaluate organization policy for compliance and assure that decisions are not contrary to Law

HRM415.title: Graduation Project
HRM415.description: This course provides an opportunity for students to employ academic tools and analysis techniques to research a project that is directly relevant to their majors and their future career. This course can be offered as a 3-credit hour course for students who wish to pursue only the classroom portion of this course and a 6-credit hour course for those who wish to combine research with an internship. The Graduation Project will include weekly classroom sessions for all students to engage in discussions related to idea generation, research techniques and data analysis. Students will also be required to attend several smaller group sessions in which they present their ideas and progress and receive feedback. Students may work individually or in teams and must deliver a case study or paper at the end of the course

HRM419.title: Internship
HRM419.description: The course requires students to complete a set number of hours in a private or public organization. Students may choose to undertake their internship in any area of business administration. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of Liwa University. Elective Courses

IDE210.title: Lean Work Design
IDE210.description: This course provides the principles and tools required to design a production system that utilizes optimal layout, material handling, workflow balance, work methods and standards, teamwork, assembly process documentation, quality control, and human factors

IDE305.title: Operations Management
IDE305.description: The course provides a foundation in fundamental concepts, techniques and applications of contemporary production and operations management to serve as tools for improving quality, productivity and international competitiveness. It covers a selection of quantitative tools and techniques to aid in decision making and operations management setting. Topics such as forecasting, product and service development, capacity planning, process selection, facility planning, quality management and inventory management will be introduced. The concepts for designing, planning and improving manufacturing and service organizations are also examined

IDE310.title: Control Systems Engineering
IDE310.description: This course introduces student to the use of hardware and software resources used to automate and control operation in manufacturing and non-manufacturing industries. Students learn to write and test relay logic circuits. Next students learn to program industrial grade PLC’s (Programmable Logic Controllers) such as Rockwell, Siemens, GE…products that are used in manufacturing to coordinate robotics, NC machines, and conveyors operations, material handling, water treatment plants, energy management operations

IDE320.title: Engineering Statistics - Statistical Inference & Regression
IDE320.description: The students are introduced to descriptive inferential, non-parametric, and inferential statistics for one and two population, contingency tables, design and analysis of single factor experiments, goodness fit tests, and regression analysis. Appropriate statistical software such as Minitab are introduced in the course

IDE330.title: Ergonomics
IDE330.description: Students are introduced to human factors and ergonomics. Problems that hinders employee’s performance due to inappropriate working environment that includes high level of noise, poor lighting, poor sanitation and safety, confusing display of information, heavy lifting, poor workflow and workplace designs and use of inappropriate tools are studied. The course topics are reinforced through laboratory exercises

IDE331.title: Ergonomics Laboratory
IDE331.description: The course deals with adequate ergonomic factors that are essential for optimal performance of work to preserve the most important assent of an enterprise: the human capital. The students implement ergonomic principles by using design, environment, skills, safety, standards and performance. The course topics are experimentally evaluated through laboratory exercises

IDE340.title: Production Planning & Control
IDE340.description: Students are introduced to the tools used to add value to the customer. Application of industrial engineering theory and practice to the area of operations management, production planning and control. Concepts in forecasting, demand and push pull production systems are to be introduced in making the value proposition to the customer

IDE350.title: System Modeling and Simulation
IDE350.description: An introduction to discrete simulation modeling design methods with emphasis of applying statistical analysis. Simulation modeling is applied to manufacturing, supply chain, transportation, and service systems. Verification and validation of simulation models. Appropriate simulation software such as Arena is used in the course

IDE370.title: Manufacturing Engineering & Industry
IDE370.description: This course introduces students to manufacturing processes, geometrical dimensioning and tolerance, computer aided manufacturing, flexible manufacturing, digital manufacturing and Industry 4.0. The course explains the important roles that modelling, simulation and optimization play which targets digital manufacturing and assembly systems for an efficient, flexible and modular production of customized products exploiting the IoT that opens the possibilities for industry 4.0

IDE400.title: Supply Chain Management
IDE400.description: Students are introduced to the tool used to manage supply chain systems. This course builds upon the concepts gained from the previous designing value in the supply chain course. Problems of complex systems with unpredictable demand forms and multiple products are studied to make quantitative based decision-making process. The PLAN, SURCE, DELIVER, and RETURN model will be used to optimize the supply chain process

IDE410.title: Operations Research I
IDE410.description: This course introduces Linear programming and formulation, graphical solution and Simplex algorithm as well as duality and sensitivity analysis. Moreover, it covers transportation, transshipment, network, and assignment models

IDE420.title: Facility Planning
IDE420.description: A comprehensive analysis of the major design issues in facilities planning of production and service facilities. The course emphasizes the use of quantitative and qualitative analysis in the design process. Topics include facility location, plant layout, materials handling, materials flow analysis, and distribution systems

IDE450.title: Quality Engineering
IDE450.description: This course introduces the tools and skill sets to solve quality problems encountered by industrial and service industries. Concepts and statistical methods employed in the assurance of product conformance to specifications, control charts for attributes and variables, proven capability analysis, acceptance of sampling plans, international standards and continuous quality improvement

IDE455.title: Project Management
IDE455.description: This course introduces students to the concepts associated with project management, and practical application of the ideas in the day-to-day planning and execution of projects. It covers all the essential aspects of project management, including creating the project scope and schedule, creating a project management plan, developing communications plan, and integration of information technology tools in project management

IDE465.title: Industrial Robotics
IDE465.description: This course introduces the use of robots in industrial settings. Robots programing to perform specific operations. Robot main and peripheral components. Safety, end-effector design, motion control, and path planning

IDE470.title: Maintenance Management
IDE470.description: This course represents a deep comprehensive study of operations and activities of maintenance and methods to manage a maintenance department in an industry. It contains an overview of maintenance functions and activities with a study of the different types and problem- solving methods of maintenance issues, including design, analysis, evaluation and control tools for maintenance management

IDE475.title: Cost Accounting and Analysis
IDE475.description: The course is intended to provide industrial engineering student with the necessary concept, tools and methods for costing products and processes. Topics include cost concept and classification, standard costing system, job order costing, activity-based costing and process costing

IDE480.title: Operations Research II
IDE480.description: This course introduces students to non-linear, integer, and modeling networks using modeling languages. The course will also be introducing advanced topics like Queuing systems and simulations on advanced software’s

IDE485.title: Decision Analysis
IDE485.description: The course overviews of modeling techniques and methods used in decision analysis, including statistical analysis, and simulation modeling analysis. Model building and analysis for practical applications through real world problems using artificial neural network are conducted

IDE490.title: Senior Design Project I
IDE490.description: This is part one of two-semester sequence courses that provides a culminating major project design experience for the students, where they propose to work on real- world problems that require the application of industrial engineering knowledge. The project needs to be approved and supervised by a faculty Supervisor. In the Senior Design Project-I course the initial phases of the project are completed, including proposal presentation, development of design requirements, identifying constraints, exploration, and evaluation of potential solutions. The teams write reports and make presentations at the end of the semester

IDE491.title: Senior Design Project II
IDE491.description: In this second part of the senior design project course sequence the project teams focus on completing their design, conduct cost analysis, and documentation. This project is a multidisciplinary interaction for industrial engineering design and management that includes system analysis and inculcates sustainable engineering principles and ethical practices. Includes use of engineering software's to complete the design, writing a technical report and developing project drawings, specifications, and details. Elective Courses

IDE495.title: Special Topics in Industrial Engineering
IDE495.description: This course covers theoretical and/or practical topics in selected areas of study within the industrial engineering discipline, beyond what is offered in existing courses to meet the interests of the students and ever-changing needs of the job market. Bachelor of Science in Data Scienc e and Artificial Intelligence Engineering Compulsory Courses

MBA501.title: Sustainability, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship
MBA501.description: This course focuses on the interrelationships between sustainability, innovation and entrepreneurship. The students will understand the effect that innovation and entrepreneurship have on the economy of the country and what they should do to fit in with the highly competitive market with an emphasis on sustainability. They will delve into the personal and professional attributes of successful entrepreneurs, including the importance of personality, experience, training, and networking. They will explore creative problem-solving, the impact of corporate culture on innovation, and the significance of ethical and socially responsible practices in entrepreneurship

MBA502.title: Applied Corporate Finance
MBA502.description: This course provides a comprehensive exploration of advanced corporate finance principles, equipping students with the skills to analyze complex financial challenges and formulate strategic solutions. Key topics include capital budgeting, valuation techniques, risk management, capital structure, and dividend policy. The course emphasizes ethical decision-making and sustainability practices, fostering responsible value creation and adherence to professional standards. Students will also engage with emerging financial technologies and advanced analytical tools to optimize corporate processes and navigate global financial markets. Designed for aspiring financial leaders, this course prepares participants to drive competitive advantage and contribute meaningfully to organizational success in dynamic and evolving business environments

MBA503.title: Advanced Managerial Accounting
MBA503.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of advanced managerial accounting concepts and techniques, emphasizing strategic decision-making and organizational success in dynamic business environments. Students will develop the ability to analyze complex business challenges, apply ethical principles, and incorporate sustainability practices into accounting decisions. Key topics include budgeting, cost management, variance analysis, transfer pricing, and advanced decision- making tools such as activity-based costing and capital budgeting. The course also focuses on the integration of advanced analytical tools and emerging technologies to optimize organizational processes, enhance resource allocation, and drive competitive advantage. Designed for advanced accounting students and professionals, this course prepares participants to address modern business challenges with a strong foundation in ethical and sustainable accounting practices

MBA504.title: Project Management
MBA504.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of project management principles, emphasizing a systems approach to planning, scheduling, and controlling projects. Students will gain insights into the roles and responsibilities of project managers, organizational structures, communication strategies, and risk management techniques. Topics include modern developments in project management, trade-off analysis, and integrating quality management. The course also incorporates practical applications of project scheduling, estimation, and leadership to ensure project success

MBA506.title: Information Technology Strategy and Management
MBA506.description: This course equips students with a thorough understanding of the recent advancements in IT as well as the key factors influencing corporate success, expansion, and sustainability. The course includes multiple real-world case studies of how companies use IT to boost production and efficiency, improve teamwork and communication, and optimize their edge over competitors. Students gain knowledge about how IT may be used to manage corporate relationships and projects, optimize systems and processes, engage and retain customers, and restructure organizations

MBA601.title: Leadership and Organizational Behavior
MBA601.description: This course introduces the Anchors of Organizational Behavior Knowledge and MARS Model of Individual Behavior and Performance. It addresses the following topics Perceiving Ourselves and Others in Organizations, Workplace Emotions, Attitudes, Stress, Foundations of Employee Motivation, Decision Making and Creativity, Leadership in Organizational Settings, Team Dynamics, Power and Influence in the Workplace, Conflict and Negotiation in the Workplace, and Organizational Change

MBA602.title: International Business Management
MBA602.description: This course introduces Key Concepts in International Business and Globalization of Markets and the Internationalization of the Firm. It covers the following topics: The Cultural Environment of International Business, Ethics, Corporate Social Responsibility, Sustainability, and Governance in International Business, Theories of International Trade and Investment. It addresses international entry strategies including Exporting and Global Sourcing, Foreign Direct Investment and Collaborative Ventures, Licensing, Franchising, and Other Contractual Strategies

MBA603.title: International Strategic Management
MBA603.description: This course focuses on international business strategy, emphasizing functional processes of international business (managing marketing, operations, HR and finance). It explores the globalization of markets and competition with emphasis on some emerging global trends underpinned by the concepts of social responsibility and sustainable development. Students will be able to evaluate country-specific opportunities, design the market entry strategies, as well as manage global mergers, acquisitions and strategic partnerships. It also delves into global human resource management, organizational design, and strategic management, equipping students with the tools to design and lead successful global organizations

MBA604.title: Operations and Supply Chain Management
MBA604.description: This course introduces the operations function and its strategic relevance to other functions, in addition to the evolution of operations and supply chain management. It addresses the concepts and decision-making tools relevant to quality management, product design, capacity and facilities design, processes and technology, facility location, inventory management, and sales and operations planning. Further, it covers supply chain management including its sustainability, integration, and performance

MBA605.title: Research Method in Business
MBA605.description: This course provides advanced insights into the research process within business context, equipping students with the skills needed to design, conduct, and present impactful business research. Students will develop a critical understanding of the research process, from formulating research questions and proposals to ethical considerations and methodological design. Emphasis is placed on practical applications, including selecting appropriate sampling techniques, employing qualitative and quantitative analysis methods such as hypothesis testing and regression, and effectively communicating findings through structured reports and presentations. The course integrates reflective practices and theoretical underpinnings to prepare students for addressing real-world business challenges with evidence-based research

MBA606.title: Marketing Management in the Digital Era
MBA606.description: This course explores the core principles of marketing management with a focus on the challenges and opportunities presented by the digital era. It emphasizes strategic decision- making and the integration of traditional and digital marketing practices to create value for organizations and their stakeholders. Topics include consumer and business market analysis, branding strategies, integrated marketing communications, pricing strategies, and the role of emerging technologies in marketing. Through case studies, projects, and practical exercises, students will develop the skills to design and implement effective marketing strategies that align with global trends and diverse consumer behaviors.
