MBA607.title: Thesis
MBA607.description: This course provides MBA students with the opportunity to conduct advanced research on real-world business challenges, emphasizing strategic problem-solving and data-driven decision-making. Through a structured thesis process, students will develop and demonstrate leadership and collaboration skills, applying ethical principles and sustainability practices to ensure responsible and impactful contributions. The course integrates advanced analytical tools and emerging business technologies, enabling participants to address global business opportunities and challenges in diverse cultural, economic, and regulatory contexts. By the end of the course, students will deliver a comprehensive thesis and oral presentation that showcase their ability to propose actionable insights and drive competitive advantage in dynamic markets. Elective Courses

MCE200.title: Introduction to Mechanical System Design
MCE200.description: This course is intended to introduce students to the fundamental concepts of machine design and mechatronics. Fundamentals of Machine Design, Phases of Design, Design Consideration – Standards and Codes – Selection of Materials –Design against Static and Dynamic Load. Mechatronic system overview: control, sensors, actuators power consideration. In addition to sensors and actuator technologies the laws pertaining to Intellectual Property are also covered. A complete team oriented open- ended design project is required. Each team will execute a design, analysis and fabrication of a prototype system

MCE210.title: Mechanics of Materials
MCE210.description: This course deals with a discussion and application of the fundamental concepts of: normal and shear stress; normal and shear strain; stress and deformation of axially loaded members; thermal stresses; torsion of circular and thin-walled sections; shear and bending moment diagrams in beams; bending in beams; transverse shear; combined loadings; stress/strain transformation; bending moment-curvature equation; deflection of beams

MCE220.title: Thermodynamics
MCE220.description: This course introduces the first and second laws of thermodynamics and their application to energy transformations during various processes. It also covers the basic properties of pure substances, ideal gases, mixture of ideal gases, and atmospheric air. Energy cycles and energy efficiencies are also discussed

MCE300.title: Dynamics
MCE300.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of dynamics (kinematics and kinetics). It starts with the study of kinematics and kinetics of a particle including relative and absolute motion. Then the analysis is extended to include the study kinematics and kinetics of rigid bodies. Topics covers force and acceleration, work-energy and impulse-momentum methods

MCE310.title: Mechanical Component Design
MCE310.description: This course Introduces students to the fundamental principles of engineering design of machine components. It involves the application of theory and techniques learned to the design of mechanical component. Formal design methodology is introduced. Topics including fatigue considerations, shaft design, threaded fasteners, lubrication and bearings, springs, and fundamentals of gear analysis are presented

MCE330.title: Heat Transfer
MCE330.description: This course introduces the basic principles of heat transfer. It covers topics of heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation. Steady-state and transient heat transfer problems, and energy conservation, fins, and analysis of heat exchangers are also covered

MCE340.title: Fluid Mechanics for Mechanical Engineers
MCE340.description: This course is and introductory course in fluid mechanics. Topics covered include fluid properties, dimensional analysis and similitude, fluid statics, Bernoulli’s equation, conservation of mass, momentum and energy, hydraulic gradient line and total energy line, linear and angular momentum equations, viscous flow in pipes, flow over immersed bodies, and concludes with introduction to compressible flows

MCE415.title: Energy and Systems Laboratory
MCE415.description: This course is a comprehensive applied study of principles and theories in fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and heat transfer. It also covers topics such as internal and external flows, pumps, aerodynamic lift and drag, fin performance, refrigeration and air conditioning and jet engine simulator

MCE435.title: Industrial Robotic and control engineering
MCE435.description: The course introduces the students to robotic that relates knowledge and skills in system and control dynamics. The course deals with frequency response analysis, kinematics or robots, differential motion, velocity, root dynamics and feedback control for design of a dynamic robotic systems used in industries

MCE440.title: Mechanical Vibrations
MCE440.description: This course introduces the techniques in extracting equations of motion for single degree and two degree of freedom systems. Students will learn how to analyze free and forced vibration systems. An introduction to Fourier transform and Fast Fourier transform is also presented in this course. Students will also learn numerical and experimental methods to analyze dynamics of structures

MCE450.title: Manufacturing Engineering
MCE450.description: This course mainly helps students to understand the physical and mechanical properties of numerous materials, manufacturing processes, economics, and quality control surrounding various recently developed manufacturing technologies and applications. It also covers fundamentals and challenges to manufacturing processes based on material properties, and design and customization of the final product

MCE451.title: Manufacturing Engineering Laboratory
MCE451.description: This course deals with physical manufacturing of engineering components. It provides the needed knowledge, simulation platform and hands-on skills to manufacturing engineering. It covers topics for mechanical tools, manual metal removal mechanisms, CNC machining and Additive Manufacturing

MCE455.title: Computer Numerical Control Machining
MCE455.description: This course introduces students to the fundamentals of CNC programming. In addition to understanding G codes, the course focuses on cutting tools, fixture set up, and manufacturing operations required to machine given materials

MCE465.title: Energy and Environment
MCE465.description: This course examines the concepts of energy conversion and conservation. Basic principles and technical details of various energy technologies (fossil, nuclear, solar, biomass, hydrogen) for the sustainable future. It discusses the different types of energies and technologies in a social context (economic, ethical, and environmental considerations

MCE470.title: Maintenance Management
MCE470.description: This course represents a deep comprehensive study of operations and activities of maintenance and methods to manage a maintenance department in an industry. It contains an overview of maintenance functions and activities with a study of the different types and problem-solving methods of maintenance issues, including design, analysis, evaluation and control tools for maintenance management

MCE472.title: Fuel cell science and engineering
MCE472.description: This course presents the engineering principles pertaining to fuel cell devices and their design. It covers topics such as fuel cell types and applications, operational parameters, efficiency, and open circuit voltages. The study also includes regulatory requirements for transporting fuel cells, as well codes and standards of operating a fuel cell powered device

MCE475.title: Introduction to Finite Element Analysis
MCE475.description: This course deals with a discussion and application of the fundamental concepts of: truss, beam and frame plane analysis using the stiffness method, plane elements, plate elements; use of available computer packages for applications in structural analysis

MCE480.title: Mechanics of Composites
MCE480.description: This is an introductory course of basic behavior of composites, properties of matrix and reinforcing materials, mechanics of fiber-reinforced composites, lamina and laminate analysis, and mechanical performance

MCE485.title: Decision Analysis
MCE485.description: The course overviews of modeling techniques and methods used in decision analysis, including statistical analysis, and simulation modeling analysis. Model building and analysis for practical applications through real world problems using artificial neural network are conducted

MCE490.title: Senior Design Project I
MCE490.description: This is part one of two-semester sequence courses that provides a culminating major project design experience for the students, where they propose to work on real-world problems that require the application of mechanical engineering knowledge. The project needs to be approved and supervised by a faculty Supervisor. In the Senior Design Project-I course the initial phases of the project are completed, including proposal presentation, development of design requirements, identifying constraints, exploration, and evaluation of potential solutions. The teams write reports and make presentations at the end of the semester

MCE491.title: Senior Design Project II
MCE491.description: In this second part of the senior design project course sequence the project teams focus on completing their design, conduct cost analysis, and documentation. This project is a multidisciplinary interaction for mechanical engineering design and management that includes system analysis and inculcates sustainable engineering principles and ethical practices. Includes use of engineering software's to complete the design, writing a technical report and developing project drawings, specifications, and details. Elective Courses

Principles of ACS diagnosis/management will be laboratory focus of this course

MDI102.title: Introduction to medical diagnostic
MDI102.description: This course provides a foundational overview of key concepts and principles essential to the field of radiography and medical imaging. Students will explore the historical development of the field, from the discovery of x-rays and radioactivity to the advent of modern imaging modalities. Emphasis will be placed on understanding fundamental patient care principles, effective communication with diverse patient populations, and the legal and safety considerations within a healthcare setting. The course will also introduce the basic principles of image production across various modalities, including radiography, fluoroscopy, computed tomography, nuclear medicine, sonography, magnetic resonance imaging, and positron emission tomography, along with the critical aspects of radiation safety and protection. from the above description please extract 6 course learning outcomes

MDI121.title: Medical Physics
MDI121.description: This course introduces fundamental physics concepts, including vectors and kinematic equations for one- and two-dimensional motions. Students will explore Newton's three Laws of Motion, with a focus on free-body diagrams, and understand the relationships between work, energy, and power. The course also covers basic conservation laws of energy and momentum and emphasizes applying mathematical techniques to solve physics problems quantitatively

MDI202.title: Radiation Biology and Radiation Protection
MDI202.description: This course includes principle of radiological biology and radiation protection The course will provide the theoretical background and training necessary for the radiological protection requirements of both ionizing and non-ionizing radiations used in hospitals

MDI211.title: Physics of Radiology
MDI211.description: This course covers fundamental concepts in medical imaging, including atomic structure, current electricity, and heat. Students will learn about x-ray production, image formation principles, and the interaction of x-ray photons with matter. The course also explores the components and operation of x-ray tubes, as well as the basics of MRI, Ultrasound, and Nuclear Medicine

MDI212.title: Digital image processing and analysis
MDI212.description: This course provides a sound understanding of the physics of Digital Radiography. It explains the principles of digital images acquisition, processing, and display

MDI214.title: Digital image processing and analysis lab
MDI214.description: This course provides hands-on experience with radiographic exposure simulations to explore the fundamental principles of digital image acquisition and processing in radiography. Students will manipulate key exposure factors such as kilovoltage (kVp), milliampere-seconds (mAs), source-to-image distance (SID), focal spot size, and patient density to understand their effects on image quality, including exposure, contrast, sharpness, and noise. Through interactive simulations and guided experiments, students will learn to optimize radiographic techniques for diagnostic accuracy while adhering to the ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) principle to minimize patient dose. The course emphasizes critical thinking and problem- solving in clinical scenarios, preparing students to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world imaging challenges

MDI216.title: Principles of Diagnostic Imaging 1
MDI216.description: This course provides an in-depth understanding of x-ray technology, covering the basic parts of the x-ray tube and the properties of x-rays. Students will learn about the consequences of scattered radiation, classify image artifacts, and describe the factors affecting radiographic image quality This course covers fundamental concepts in medical imaging, including atomic structure, current electricity, and heat. Students will learn about x-ray production, image formation principles, and the interaction of x-ray photons with matter. The course also explores the components and operation of x-ray tubes, as well as the basics of MRI, Ultrasound, and Nuclear Medicine

MDI218.title: Principles of Diagnostic Imaging 1 -Lab
MDI218.description: This course introduces the student to radiologic technology science and explains the process of image formation including radiographic film structure, latent image formation, and processing of the x- ray film. In addition, it describes the factors which affect image quality

MDI224.title: Peripheral osseous system radiography
MDI224.description: This course includes demonstration and practice in positioning and anatomical radiography of the upper and lower extremities to include shoulder and pelvic girdles

MDI226.title: Peripheral osseous system radiography lab
MDI226.description: This course includes demonstration and practice in positioning and anatomical radiography of the upper and lower extremities to include shoulder and pelvic girdles

MDI228.title: Patient Care in Radiology Department
MDI228.description: This course provides the foundation knowledge and skills that students need to provide safe and effective patient care as a student health practitioner. The course introduced the medico- legal and ethical responsibilities of a medical imaging practitioner. Students will be able to integrate the physical, mental, and psychosocial aspects of care to provide a holistic approach to interacting with and caring for patients. students will be able to apply infection control and manuals. handling techniques and conduct basic patient assessments. The course also introduced the common medical emergencies that may occur in the medical imaging clinical environment

MDI230.title: Patient Care in Radiology Department Lab
MDI230.description: This course provides the foundation knowledge and skills that students need to provide safe and effective patient care as a student health practitioner. The course introduced the medico- legal and ethical responsibilities of a medical imaging practitioner. Students will be able to integrate the physical, mental, and psychosocial aspects of care to provide a holistic approach to interacting with and caring for patients. students will be able to apply infection control and manuals. handling techniques and conducting basic patient assessments. The course also introduced the common medical emergencies that may occur in the medical imaging clinical environment

MDI311.title: Principles of Diagnostic Imaging 2
MDI311.description: This course explains the process of image intensification, fluoroscopic and imaging equipment, also include deep explanation of the conventional tomographic procedure, magnification radiography, stereoradiography, mammography and soft tissue imaging, digital imaging technique, and formulating the x-ray technique chart

MDI313.title: Principles of Diagnostic Imaging 2 lab
MDI313.description: This lab introduces the process of image intensification, fluoroscopic and imaging equipment. It also explains the conventional tomographic procedure, magnification radiography, stereoradiography, mammography and soft tissue imaging, digital imaging technique, and formulating the x-ray technique chart

MDI327.title: Central osseous system radiography
MDI327.description: This course provides the student with instruction in the radiographic anatomy and positioning of the skull, facial bone, sinuses, mastoids, temporal bones, vertebral columns, and thorax. Students will be required to participate in simulation activities on each other for each of the procedures covered in this course

MDI329.title: Central Osseous System Radiography Lab
MDI329.description: This course provides the student with instruction in the radiographic anatomy and positioning and to obtain basic knowledge, skills, and application of alignment of body parts, cassettes, and x-ray tube in each elementary radiographic examination correlated with patient care procedures. Emphasis will be placed on positioning terms, projections of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, skull, facial bone, sinuses, chest, abdomen, pelvis and vertebral column. As well as corresponding radiographic analysis. A laboratory component is included. Student will be required to participate in simulation activities on each other for each of the procedures covered in this course

MDI333.title: Radiographic surface anatomy
MDI333.description: In this course, students gain knowledge that will assist in the development of their ability to correctly identify and localize human anatomy in radiographic images. The course serves as a foundation for the progression towards clinical competencies knowledge; it also provides an awareness of common anomalies. The course covers the chest, abdomen, pelvis, skull, upper and lower extremities, vertebral column radiographic anatomy and routine fluoroscopic procedures

MDI334.title: Radiographic cross-sectional anatomy
MDI334.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of human anatomy as visualized through cross-sectional imaging modalities such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Students will learn to identify anatomical structures in axial, coronal, and sagittal planes, with emphasis on the thorax, abdominopelvic region, and neuroanatomy (brain, cranium, and facial bones). Topics include imaging principles, contrast usage, advanced visualization techniques (e.g., multiplanar reformatting, volume rendering), and the application of anatomical knowledge to interpret clinical images. The course integrates theoretical foundations with practical skills (the corequisite MDI 336 Course) to prepare students for roles in medical imaging and diagnostic radiology

MDI335.title: Enter internal Course Code
MDI335.description: In this course, students gain knowledge that will assist in the development of their ability to correctly identify and localize human anatomy in radiographic images. The course serves as a foundation for the progression towards clinical competencies knowledge; it also provides an awareness of common anomalies. The course covers the chest, abdomen, pelvis, skull, upper and lower extremities, vertebral column radiographic anatomy and routine fluoroscopic procedures

MDI336.title: Radiographic cross sectional anatomy lab
MDI336.description: This course study of human anatomy as seen in axial, sagittal, and coronal planes as would be shown on CT or MRI examinations. Bony, muscular, vascular, soft tissues, and organs of the following anatomical regions are studied: central nervous system, cardiovascular, thorax, abdomen, and pelvis

MDI346.title: Radiologic Pathology
MDI346.description: This course is a comprehensive discussion of various pathological processes that affect various body systems and their radiological appearances

MDI350.title: Breast Imaging
MDI350.description: This course introduces the students to the process of breast imaging. It exposes the student to the physical principle of mammography and its clinical applications. The imaging procedure is covered in addition to the quality assurances and troubleshooting

MDI352.title: Fluoroscopic imaging
MDI352.description: This course introduces the student to the applications of contrast media (CM) in radiography. It provides an explicit description of the fluoroscopic procedures for the different body systems including the gastrointestinal tract (GIT), urinary system and female reproductive system, salivary glands etc…. It also introduces the student to the different types of contrast media used in fluoroscopy and their side effects

MDI354.title: Fluoroscopic imaging lab
MDI354.description: This course introduces the student to the applications of contrast media (CM) in radiography. It provides an explicit description of the fluoroscopic procedures for the different body systems including the gastrointestinal tract (GIT), urinary system and female reproductive system, salivary glands etc…. It also introduces the student to the different types of contrast media used in fluoroscopy and their side effects

MDI356.title: Dental radiography
MDI356.description: Study of the basic intraoral and extraoral radiographic projections that are used in dentistry. Study of various techniques of image production, and new advances in dental radiography. Emphasis on radiation protection (operator and patient). Focus on radiographic interpretation, client management, mounting procedures and quality assurance

MDI362.title: Ultrasound
MDI362.description: This course introduces the students to the process of breast imaging. It exposes the student to the physical principle of mammography and its clinical applications. The imaging procedure is covered in addition to the quality assurances and troubleshooting

MDI376.title: Nuclear medicine
MDI376.description: This comprehensive course in Nuclear Medicine Technology integrates theoretical knowledge and practical skills essential for the safe and effective use of radiopharmaceuticals in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Topics include radiation physics, decay calculations, instrumentation (e.g., scintillation cameras, PET/CT scanners), and imaging techniques such as SPECT and PET. Emphasis is placed on radiation safety (ALARA principles), regulatory compliance, radiopharmaceutical preparation, quality control, and patient care. The course also covers clinical applications across body systems (e.g., CNS, endocrine, cardiovascular, skeletal) and addresses cultural competence, HIPAA compliance, and ethical considerations in patient interactions. Students will gain proficiency in performing calculations, operating imaging systems, and adhering to protocols for radiation protection and contamination control

MDI385.title: Internship I
MDI385.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the clinical environment and provide them with the opportunity to interact with staff radiographers and radiologists to begin developing clinical skills. Students begin developing critical thinking and problem-solving skills in the clinical areas as they begin to perform upper extremity, lower extremity and shoulder examinations learned in the classroom and practiced in the laboratory setting. Staff radiographers directly supervise students during this period

MDI413.title: Quality control in medical imaging
MDI413.description: This course delves into the principles of quality management, quality assurance, and quality control in medical imaging. Students will learn to differentiate between these concepts, list the benefits of quality control for patients and departments, discuss the proper tests and tools used in quality control, and evaluate the results of these tests

MDI415.title: Quality control in medical imaging lab
MDI415.description: This course is designed to cover all the technical and administrative processes to ensure that radiographic equipment performs according to manufacturing standards

MDI419.title: Graduation Project
MDI419.description: This course involves individual student research work, including a literature search and the creation of a study plan in collaboration with a supervisor. At the end, students will write a research report and design, present, and discuss a poster based on their results

MDI453.title: Vascular Imaging
MDI453.description: This course is an introduction to catheter-based angiographic procedures, covering the technological and practical aspects of angiography and cardiac catheterization. It also introduces students to major interventional procedures and prepares them for clinical training in their fourth year

MDI455.title: Vascular Imaging Lab
MDI455.description: This course is an introduction to catheter-based angiographic procedures. It covers the technological and practical aspects of angiography and cardiac catheterization and introduces students to major interventional procedures. The course is designed to prepare students for clinical training in their fourth year

MDI463.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
MDI463.description: This course provides the physics related to obtaining CT images, including information on data acquisition, processing, hardware, software, and technical parameters. It also covers the scanning procedures necessary to obtain CT images of anatomical structures and organs

MDI465.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Lab non- Arabic
MDI465.description: This course introduces the student to the principles of MRI, including physical and clinical aspects of the imaging process. The physical part covers topics like magnetization, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), image contrast formation, pulse sequences, flow phenomena, and image artifacts. The clinical aspect provides basic knowledge of imaging protocols and parameters for areas like the head, neck, spine, chest, abdomen, pelvis, and limbs

MDI467.title: Computed Tomography
MDI467.description: This course introduces the student to the principles of MRI, covering both physical and clinical aspects. The physical part includes magnetization, NMR, image contrast formation, pulse sequences, and safety. The clinical part provides basic knowledge of imaging protocols and parameters for different parts of the body, such as the head and neck, spine, chest, abdomen, pelvis, and limbs

MDI469.title: Computed Tomography
MDI469.description: This course provides the physics related to obtaining CT images. It includes information on data acquisition, processing, hardware, software, and technical parameters. The course also covers the scanning procedures needed to get CT images of anatomical structures and organs

MDI487.title: Internship II
MDI487.description: The Clinical Internships course series is designed to provide students with hands-on, practical experience in medical diagnostic imaging. Over three levels, students will progressively develop their clinical skills, apply theoretical knowledge in real- world settings, and gain exposure to various imaging modalities and patient care scenarios. Each level builds on the previous one, enhancing the student's competence and confidence in performing diagnostic imaging procedures. This course consolidates to perform Specialized advanced imaging procedures & techniques, Interventional radiography (vascular & non-vascular applications), and CT Scan imaging (advanced applications in systemic imaging, advanced image processing, contrast media usage & optimization, image quality versus radiation dose, dose optimization techniques, advanced/abnormal cross sectional anatomy and image evaluation & interpretation)

MDI488.title: Internship III
MDI488.description: The Clinical Internships course series is designed to provide students with hands-on, practical experience in medical diagnostic imaging. Over three levels, students will progressively develop their clinical skills, apply theoretical knowledge in real- world settings, and gain exposure to various imaging modalities and patient care scenarios. Each level builds on the previous one, enhancing the student's competence and confidence in performing diagnostic imaging procedures. This course consolidates to perform radiographic modalities Quality Assurance Procedures, clinical applications of the MRI, nuclear medicine & Ultrasound. Bachelor of Science in Medical Laboratory Analysis (BS-MLA)

MKT200.title: Introduction to Marketing
MKT200.description: This course introduces the students to basic marketing concepts and terminology and integrates learning material with real world examples. Areas covered include: the marketing concept, marketing mix, the marketing environment, marketing information and research, consumer behavior, pricing strategies and market segmentation

MKT202.title: Consumer Information
MKT202.description: This course covers the role of marketing research in consumer behaviour and decision making. Emphasis is placed on both the establishment of theories of CB, together with their practical application and how these behaviours and theories are researched in practice. In all cases the cultural significance of the UAE will be paramount. At the heart of this course is an independent research project, which will take the majority of the semester to complete. It will be based on some aspect of current consumer behaviour and will be fully defined and researched during the time the course is taking place. By the time it is completed, the student will have mastered an array of extremely valuable skills and knowledge bases. Some of the indicative types of projects might include: •An examination of the motivation to purchase high brand jeans. •Brand loyalty among restaurant goers in Abu Dhabi. •Perceptual mapping of Universities in the •Celebrity endorsement in the UAE

MKT203.title: Service Marketing
MKT203.description: The purpose of this course is to introduce marketing services as a separate and distinct area of marketing thought and practice and assist in understanding their powerful influence in competitive markets. During this course we focus our attention on marketing services based upon an in-depth understanding of the service customer, realizing that there can be various types of customers in a service environment. We also discuss an overarching philosophy that stresses the importance of the integration of marketing, human resources, and operations within the service system. All course activities are intended to help students become proficient in analyzing and judging the merits of services marketing strategies and assist in making strategic decisions in both business and consumer services industries. Throughout the course an emphasis is placed on marketing's role within the total organization.The purpose of this course is to introduce marketing services as a separate and distinct area of marketing thought and practice and assist in understanding their powerful influence in competitive markets. We also discuss an overarching philosophy that stresses the importance of the integration of marketing, human resources, and operations within the service system.
