Throughout the course an emphasis is placed on marketing's role within the total organization. BBA in Marketing- Concentration in Digital Marketing Major Courses

MKT204.title: Personal Selling
MKT204.description: This course focuses on the application of behavioral and persuasive communication theories and techniques necessary to develop effective personal selling skills within an organization. Emphasis on personal and professional development, interpersonal skills, verbal and written presentation skills, understanding business prospects, selling and buying processes, and developing and maintaining customer satisfaction

MKT301.title: Consumer Behavior
MKT301.description: This course is an introduction to the world of consumer behavior. The discipline derives from several social sciences including psychology, sociology, and marketing to explain the behavior of the customer in the marketplace. In this course, the student will understand how personality, perceptions, learning, and attitudes affect consumption behavior. Additionally, to explore how consumption changes during one’s life cycle, and how powerful cultural and subcultural influences are on consumers

MKT302.title: Market Research
MKT302.description: This course covers the role of marketing research in marketing decision making. Emphasis is placed on marketing research within the context of the UAE business environment and the use of the internet as a research tool. The course covers definition of research problems, selection of research methodologies, design of research projects, interpretation of research results, and translation of research results into action. The heart of this course is an independent research project, which will take the entire semester to complete. By the time it is completed, the student will have mastered an array of extremely valuable skills

MKT304.title: International Marketing
MKT304.description: This course is designed to provide students with an overview of the international marketing arena. The course deals with all aspects of marketing from an international perspective and prepares the students to deal with foreign competitive situations and internal opportunities. It offers practical exposure to marketing challenges faces by the multinational businesses through case studies and scenarios which relate to several areas of marketing (market research, marketing management, sales- force management, and marketing communications...) and international marketing

MKT305.title: Consumer Communication
MKT305.description: To enable students, develop a thorough understanding of brand development and IMC management theory including key concepts such as brand positioning and movement, measurement of brand values, and translation of brand benefits into tangible outputs. This course will help students understand the opportunity and threats posed by brand development and IMC management including the study of relevant buyer behavior concepts, brand creation and development, media messages, resources and budgets, creative translation of brand values, and effectiveness measurements as they relate to the management tasks of developing, implementing, and evaluating promotional strategies

MKT351.title: E-Marketing
MKT351.description: The internet and other information technologies have created many interesting and innovative ways to provide customer value since its inception in 1969. Web sites for marketing communication and customer support; one-to-one communication to many different receiving devices; consumer behavior insights based on offline and online data combination; inventory optimization through CRM-SCM integration; a single- minded focus on ROI and associated performance metrics are all important strategies. The social media provide perfect platforms for connecting with today’s consumer: High readership blogs, social networks (such as Facebook and LinkedIn), and online communities (such as YouTube, Twitter and Second Life), gave consumers the opportunity to be heard in large numbers, and smart marketers have learned how to tap into these “citizen journalists” for improving products and marketing communication. Students will learn all about these strategies and more in this course. The course uses a mix of lecture/discussion, interesting individual and group projects, and exams. Prepare for an exciting and dynamic learning experience

MKT473.title: Social Media Marketing
MKT473.description: This course explores the pivotal role of social media marketing as a fundamental element of contemporary business strategies aimed at engaging and retaining customers. Students will gain an in-depth understanding of both strategic and practical aspects of social media marketing, covering key areas such as social media planning, content creation, audience targeting, performance measurement, and campaign optimization. The curriculum delves into social media platforms, buyer personas, and strategic goal setting while leveraging analytics and key performance indicators (KPIs) to drive data-informed decisions. Emphasis is placed on integrating social media efforts with broader marketing objectives, focusing on emerging trends, tools, and technologies shaping the social media landscape

MLS110.title: Clinical Laboratory Instrumentation
MLS110.description: This course aims to introduce the practical applications of clinical laboratory instruments and introduces the students to the principles of instrumental methods of analysis including visible and ultraviolet spectrophotometry, flame photometry, chromatography, electrophoresis, radiation counters and automated chemical analyzers. The student will be exposed to sophisticated analytical instruments to enhance laboratory skills and confidence of working in the medical laboratory

MLS210.title: Clinical Chemistry I
MLS210.description: This course is designed to introduce the student to diagnosis and monitoring of disease using plasma, serum, urine, and other body fluids. Student will gain knowledge and skills in various analytical techniques and methods used in the measurement of various parameters in the blood and other body fluids, and to gain technical skills and knowledge of interpretation of test results in health and disease states. The course mostly covers routine laboratory investigations related to disorders of plasma proteins and amino acids, carbohydrate disorders, lipids and lipoprotein abnormalities, enzymes, blood gases and electrolytes

MLS211.title: Medical Microbiology
MLS211.description: This course focuses on the foundation of the basic principles of medical microbiology. The course is designed to provide Medical Laboratory Sciences students with adequate knowledge about microbes, diseases, modes of transmission of infections and infection control measures applied in the context of UAE. The course involves identification of the role of saprophytes, normal commensal flora, and pathogenic microbes that cause common infectious diseases in UAE. The course elaborates the tools and methods for the study of microbes, microbial structure and function, virulence factors as well as microbial genetics and its importance in the virulence of microbes are also dealt with in the course. The basic immune defense mechanism of the host is also considered in this course. Students in practical sessions will experience preparation of bacterial culture media, sterilization and antiseptic techniques and an antibiotic sensitivity test as applied in clinical laboratories within the UAE

MLS212.title: Basic Hematology
MLS212.description: This course is designed to introduce the theoretical and practical aspects of normal hematology and will include the normal composition of blood, collection and storage of blood, hemopoiesis, morphology, structure, and function of red cells, white cells and platelets in addition to the normal hemostasis. The course will provide students with knowledge and skills to perform a variety of lab tests and to know the different components of the blood

MLS213.title: Immunology
MLS213.description: This course is designed to introduce the student to the fundamentals of this specialized branch of laboratory medicine. It involves the study of the process of immunity, theory, and practice of a wide variety of procedures used in the laboratory. The composites of Innate and Adaptive immunity are discussed and how they interact in recognizing foreign molecules to defend the body against invading microorganisms. Practical aspects of antigen and antibody interactions are investigated

MLS220.title: Histology and Microtechniques
MLS220.description: This course is designed to introduce the students to concepts of histology related to the cells and tissue , arrangements of the human body, It deal with the study of the micro anatomical structure and function of the body’s major organs of the epithelial; connective; muscular and nervous tissues; structural and functional relationships between cells and tissues in organs; comparative histology of the circulatory; nervous; digestive; integumentary; respiratory; excretory; reproductive; endocrine and sensory systems , laboratory exercises will include the study of prepared slides and of micro techniques; practice on standard methods of microscopic slide preparation

MLS221.title: Clinical chemistry II
MLS221.description: This course is designed to introduce the student to the various analytical techniques and methods used in the measurement of various parameters in the blood and other body fluids, and to gain technical skills and knowledge of interpretation of test results in health and disease states. The course mostly covers routine laboratory investigations related to disorders such as cardiac function, kidney function, liver function, hormonal abnormalities, pancreatic function, and gastrointestinal disorders

MLS222.title: Diagnostic Hematology
MLS222.description: This course is designed to provide the student with knowledge and practical skills used for differential diagnosis of erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets, and hemostatic inherited/acquired disorders. Erythrocyte disorders include anemias, hemoglobinopathies, and metabolic anemias. Leukocyte disorders include benign leukocyte disorders, chronic and acute leukemia, proliferative disorders, and hemostatic disorders including platelets disorders (thrombocytosis and thrombocytopenia), vascular disorders, fibrinolytic system disorders and coagulation disorders (hypercoagulable abnormalities and bleeding tendency). Laboratory morphology and additional tests used in the diagnosis of these disorders play an integral role in this course as well as the correlation of clinical and laboratory data

MLS223.title: Transfusion Science
MLS223.description: This course introduces the students to the history of blood transfusion and discovery of blood group systems. Inheritance and clinical significance of major blood group systems and their applications in transfusion medicine is discussed together with the techniques of antibody detection and antigen typing. Emphasis is also placed on blood bank techniques including blood grouping, antigen typing, and Anti-human globulin testing. Donor selection and processing, blood component preparation, storage and expiry and indications for use are discussed. Adverse effects of blood transfusion are discussed as well as the pathophysiology and management of Haemolytic Disease of the Newborn (HDNB) and Auto Immune Hemolytic Anaemia (AIHA). Laboratory exercises include grouping and matching techniques, antibody detection and identification, and other procedures associated with blood bank practice

MLS225.title: Clinical Practice
MLS225.description: Clinical Practice is an integral part of the program in Associate Degree in Medical Laboratory Analysis and is designed to provide graduating students with an opportunity to integrate and apply previously acquired knowledge and technical skills in clinical settings. Under the guidance of experienced Medical Laboratory Professionals and other qualified laboratory preceptors, students learn more about diagnostic test procedures, quality control methods and programs, and instrumentation in the pre- analytical, analytical and post-analytical clinical laboratory. Students also gain an understanding of the roles and functions of the Medical Laboratory Professionals. The Clinical Practice program is conducted in an affiliated hospital laboratory, where students learn by participating in the workload of a supervising preceptor. Students will be equally rotated in four disciplines; Clinical chemistry, Hematology, Microbiology and Histopathology. The focus of this course is on laboratory practice and laboratory organization. The course will introduce students to professional etiquette and health and safety in the clinical laboratories. It will also cover the reception and processing of clinical samples and observation of the most commonly used techniques in each laboratory. The course gives students practical experience in effective communications to ensure accurate and appropriate information transfer. Finally, it helps students find employment by gaining experience they require to enter the world of medical laboratory diagnosis. Diploma in Emergency Medical Care

MLS310.title: Hematology: Coagulation & Hemostasis
MLS310.description: This course describes the mechanisms of normal hemostasis and the roles and interactions of blood vessels, platelets, coagulation and fibrinolytic systems. The inherited and acquired disorders of hemostasis will be studied, and students will carry out the practical tasks needed to differentiate and diagnose these disorders. The causes and clinical effects of thrombosis will be discussed. Students will carry out the appropriate laboratory tests involved in the diagnosis and treatment of these disorders

MLS311.title: Clinical Parasitology
MLS311.description: The course aims at familiarizing students with the basic concepts of Parasitology, types of animal associations, adaptations to parasitic mode of life and evolution of parasitism. Parasites’ life – cycles, infection, transmission, pathology, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, and control of medically and economically important parasites are the main emphasis of this course. Laboratory sessions are designed to expose the students to the morphology of the different developmental stages of medical and economically important parasites as well as introducing the skills of proper laboratory procedures for collecting, handling, diagnosing, and identifying parasitic organisms

MLS312.title: Diagnostic Microbiology I
MLS312.description: This course focuses on systemic pathogenic bacteria. This course provides students with theoretical and practical aspects of various groups of bacteria their classification, morphology, cultural characters, biochemical reactions, resistance, antigenic structure, virulence factors, pathogenicity, clinical features, laboratory diagnosis, treatment and epidemiology. The principles of culture, identification and susceptibility testing are covered in depth using live cultures of various Gram positive and Gram-negative bacteria to encompass all areas of systematic bacteriology. Special focus is also given to antimicrobial chemotherapy which includes their classification based on bacterial anatomical targets, mechanism of action, resistance and antibiotic susceptibility testing

MLS320.title: Urinalysis & Body Fluids
MLS320.description: This course is intended to provide the student with a foundation for performing urine and body fluid analysis. The anatomy and physiology of the renal system, urine formation, chemical analysis of urine and the microscopic examination of urinary sediment will be introduced. Urinary and metabolic diseases as they relate to urinalysis findings will be discussed. An introduction to body fluids and their clinical significance will be examined

MLS321.title: Principle of Human Genetics
MLS321.description: This course is designed to introduce the student to the study of biological inheritance in humans, the history and principles of heredity at the molecular and cellular level, and the transmission and expression of genetic information. The course enables an improved understanding of genetics topics and their influence on modern life such as the structure of DNA and RNA, gene expression, gene organization, gene regulation and gene transfer. Current issues such as recombinant DNA technology, human heritable diseases and population genetics are included. The course provides a foundation for studies in human biology and related fields regarding the principles of inheritance, structure and function of genetic material, prokaryotic and eukaryotic genes and finally the impact of genetics on population dynamics and evolution

MLS322.title: Diagnostic Microbiology II
MLS322.description: This course is the study of microorganisms of medical importance in relationship to disease and diagnosis. This course also emphasizes identification of bacteria in patient specimens, specimen collection and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. The course will provide the conceptual basis for understanding pathogenic microorganisms and particularly address the fundamental mechanisms of their pathogenicity. The laboratory sessions cover techniques of identification of normal flora, pathogenic bacteria, including morphology, classification and cultivation of bacteria

MLS323.title: Clinical Immunology and Serology
MLS323.description: This course provides a foundation in the theoretical basis of clinical immunology and will give the student an understanding of the mechanisms of diagnostic tests, interpretation of results of immunological tests, and the clinical settings in which various tests are appropriate. The laboratory portion of this course will provide an opportunity for the student to perform directed exercises in clinical immunology. These exercises will teach basic techniques in clinical immunology, provide a practical link to the theoretical information present in lecture and show the divers applications of immunological techniques

MLS410.title: Molecular Biology
MLS410.description: This course provides knowledge and understanding of traditional and molecular genetics and molecular biology. It examines advanced aspects of genetics and inheritance at a phenotypic, population and molecular level. It also provides basic skills on molecular biology techniques The course introduces the student to be familiar with the basic molecular biology regarding the DNA structure and function, RNA structure and function through the molecular biology central dogma (replication, transcription, and translation) and application of the molecular biology techniques in laboratory diagnosis. By the end of the course the student should be familiar with and gain an understanding of the objectives, applicability and limitations underlying each of these methods. Includes the analysis of nucleic acids: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR), gel electrophoresis and blotting techniques (Northern, Southern), real-time PCR, microarrays (DNA chips), DNA sequencing and methods to study gene function. Manipulation and analysis of gene expression in prokaryotic systems, through eukaryotic tools

MLS411.title: Medical Virology
MLS411.description: The course introduces the basic principles of virology including definitions, structure, nomenclature, classifications, modes of viral infection, viral diseases and viral vaccines. Also, the course designed to introduce student to the major classes of viruses and their replication mechanisms, to examine virus-host interactions, and to discuss the public health aspects of virus infections, as well as major systemic diseases cause by various viruses. The practical part of the course will provide students with fundamental virology laboratory techniques

MLS412.title: Laboratory Management and Quality Assurance
MLS412.description: This is an integrated course of both laboratory management and quality assurance in the medical laboratory. The course describes the fundamental principles and practices of management and supervision of clinical laboratory including management of organizations, human resources, financial resources, and laboratory operations. Concerning quality assurance, the course covers subjects related to quality concepts and terminology, tools of quality monitoring and assessment, data interpretation, and appropriate actions in response to QC results

MLS419.title: Graduation Project
MLS419.description: This course provides students with the opportunity to apply research skills and carry out a research project related to the major program under the supervision of a faculty member. Students will be required to conduct literature review and perform data collection, statistical analysis, writing up of the research paper. Students participating in research must complete CITI program (https://about.citiprogram.org/en/homepage/) for research ethics and compliance training prior to submitting research proposals

MLS420.title: Clinical Practice
MLS420.prerequisites: MLS 220, MLS 221, MLS 222, MLS 223, MLS 310, MLS 311, MLS 320, MLS 323, MLS 410, MLS 411, MLS 412
MLS420.description: Clinical Practice is an integral part of the program in Medical Laboratory Analysis and is designed to provide graduating students with an opportunity to integrate and apply previously acquired knowledge and technical skills in clinical settings. Under the guidance of experienced Medical Laboratory Professionals and other qualified laboratory preceptors, students learn more about diagnostic test procedures, quality control methods and programs, and instrumentation in the pre- analytical, analytical, and post-analytical clinical laboratory. Students also gain an understanding of the roles and functions of the Medical Laboratory Professionals. The Clinical Practice program is conducted in an affiliated hospital laboratory, where students learn by participating in the workload of a supervising preceptor. The course gives students practical experience in effective communications to ensure accurate and appropriate information transfer. Finally, it helps students find employment by gaining experience they require to enter the world of medical laboratory. Bachelor of Science in Occupational Therapy

MTH105.title: Mathematics and Statistics
MTH105.description: This course introduces some mathematical concepts needed for success and facing this century life. It covers different topics like; basic concepts of mathematics, such as ratios and proportions, general algebra, linear equations, and linear and exponential functions by graphing them. Additionally, it covers the basic concepts of statistics and how to analyze statistical results

MTH110.title: Calculus I
MTH110.description: Calculus is an exciting subject, justly considered to be one of the greatest achievements of the human intellect. Today calculus is used not just in the physical sciences, but also in engineering, business, economics, life sciences, and social sciences—any discipline that seeks to understand dynamic phenomena. Part of the aim of this course is to train the student to think logically. Learn to write the solutions of the exercises in a connected, step- by-step fashion with explanatory sentences—not just a string of disconnected equations or formulas. This course is intended to introduce derivatives, one of the two key concepts of calculus. The second is integral. Both key concepts depend on the notion of limit

MTH203.title: Business Statistics
MTH203.description: This course will introduce the learner to some techniques in descriptive and inferential statistics. Topics included are data presentation using different tools, central measures, dispersion measures, introduction to probability, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression, and computer applications

OT200.title: Foundations of Occupational Therapy
OT200.description: This foundational course covers the principles, history, and ethics of occupational therapy (OT), introducing students to the profession's role in the healthcare field. The practical component involves case-based discussions where students analyze real- world applications of OT in clinical settings, highlighting innovation in therapeutic approaches to enhance patient care and adaptability in modern healthcare systems

OT201.title: Patient Assessment (Functional Assessment of OT)
OT201.description: This course focuses on developing the skills necessary for conducting functional assessments in occupational therapy. The course covers a wide range of assessment tools and techniques used to evaluate a patient’s functional abilities, including activities of daily living (ADLs), mobility, cognitive functioning, and overall independence. The theoretical component will explore the principles of assessment, test selection, and interpretation, with an emphasis on evidence-based practices and innovative approaches that promote sustainable patient care. The practical component will provide students with hands- on experience in conducting assessments with real patients, fostering adaptability, creativity, and sustainable use of resources in therapeutic practice. This course aims to prepare students to gather and analyze data, identify areas of need, and develop effective intervention plans to improve patient outcomes in a responsible and forward-looking manner

OT202.title: OT Process and Techniques
OT202.description: Students will explore the occupational therapy process, covering assessment, intervention, and evaluation of outcomes. The course includes practical lab sessions where students will practice therapeutic techniques and use various tools. It addresses the entire OT process, from referral to discharge, emphasizing the design of patient-centered and sustainable intervention plans, and the application of innovative techniques in simulated clinical settings. Students will assess the effectiveness of interventions based on client progress and work collaboratively to enhance their skills, adaptability, and decision- making. Ethical considerations, professional standards, and innovative approaches to ensure sustainable healthcare outcomes are also integral parts of the curriculum

OT203.title: Neuroscience
OT203.description: This course introduces students to the structure and function of the nervous system, with an emphasis on how neurological dysfunctions influence occupational performance. The practical component integrates case studies and hands-on applications of neuroscience principles in occupational therapy practice, highlighting innovative therapeutic strategies that promote patient adaptation, recovery, and long-term well-being in diverse clinical contexts

OT300.title: Human Growth and Development
OT300.description: This course examines human development from infancy through old age, emphasizing the ways in which biological, psychological, and social changes affect occupational performance. Students will explore typical and atypical developmental patterns and analyze the role of occupational therapy in supporting clients at each stage of life. The course also highlights innovative and sustainable approaches to promote lifelong adaptation, well- being, and inclusion in diverse environments

OT301.title: OT Theories and Techniques
OT301.description: This course covers the theoretical models that guide occupational therapy (OT) practice, including the Kawa Model and the Person-Environment-Occupation (PEO) Model. Students will apply these models to case studies during practical sessions to strengthen their clinical reasoning skills. The course also emphasizes innovative approaches and sustainable applications of OT models, enabling learners to deliver culturally sensitive, holistic, and client-centered interventions that adapt to evolving healthcare needs

OT302.title: Functional Assessment of OT
OT302.prerequisites: OT 201 Students will deepen their knowledge of functional assessment tools and techniques, gaining the ability to evaluate client performance across diverse contexts. The practical component emphasizes hands-on application of these assessments, such as evaluating mobility and dexterity in various client populations. The course also integrates innovative assessment strategies and sustainable practices to ensure accurate, ethical, and long-term applicability of functional evaluations in occupational therapy

OT303.title: Biomechanics
OT303.description: This course covers the principles of biomechanics as they relate to occupational therapy. Students will learn to assess clients’ movement patterns and identify dysfunctions that affect daily functioning. Practical sessions will involve designing and implementing interventions to improve function, prevent injury, and enhance performance in activities of daily living. The course also emphasizes the integration of innovative biomechanical strategies and sustainable rehabilitation practices to support long-term health, independence, and occupational engagement

OT304.title: Hand Splinting
OT304.description: This course teaches students the theory and application of hand splinting for a variety of upper extremity conditions. In practical sessions, students will design, fabricate, and fit splints, developing their clinical reasoning and problem-solving skills to meet client needs. The course also emphasizes the use of innovative splinting techniques and sustainable material choices to ensure effective, client-centered interventions that balance functionality, comfort, and long-term usability

OT305.title: Applied OT for Neurological Conditions
OT305.description: Students will examine how common neurological conditions impact occupational performance and develop patient-centered interventions for individuals with neurological impairments. The course features practical lab sessions to apply neurorehabilitation techniques aimed at promoting functional recovery. Students will assess the effectiveness of these interventions and collaborate with peers to tailor techniques to meet diverse client needs

OT307.title: Upper Extremity Rehabilitation
OT307.description: This course covers the assessment and treatment techniques for upper extremity injuries and conditions affecting the shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand. Students will apply advanced rehabilitation techniques in practical settings to restore functional abilities and enhance occupational performance in clients with upper extremity disorders. The course emphasizes innovative therapeutic strategies and sustainable rehabilitation practices to promote recovery, long-term independence, and improved quality of life

OT400.title: Community-Based Rehabilitation
OT400.description: This course examines the role of occupational therapy in community-based rehabilitation (CBR) programs, with a focus on delivering healthcare services to underserved and marginalized communities. Students will learn to design, implement, and evaluate CBR projects that promote community participation, health equity, and sustainable well-being. The practical component provides hands-on experience in creating and managing CBR initiatives that address the unique needs of vulnerable populations, incorporating innovative strategies to strengthen inclusion, resilience, and long-term impact

OT401.title: OT Process and Techniques
OT401.description: This course introduces students to the principles and applications of assistive technology in occupational therapy, with a focus on mobility aids, communication devices, and environmental modifications. It covers evaluation, activity analysis, and intervention processes with a range of assistive technologies, including software, hardware, and low-tech solutions. The course emphasizes innovative and sustainable approaches to adapting activities and contexts, equipping students with the skills to select and apply assistive technologies that promote independence, accessibility, and long-term usability. The practical component provides hands-on experience in tailoring assistive technologies to meet diverse client needs

OT402.title: Pediatrics and Psychiatric Cases (Special Patient Populations)
OT402.description: This course focuses on occupational therapy interventions for pediatric and psychiatric populations, addressing their unique developmental and psychosocial needs. It examines the etiology, diagnosis, prognosis, clinical presentation, functional limitations, and common treatments and medications associated with these conditions. Students will explore a variety of frames of reference, evaluative strategies, and intervention approaches for children and their families in medical, home, community, and educational settings. The course emphasizes innovative therapeutic practices and sustainable approaches to promote inclusion, resilience, and long-term well-being. The practical component includes simulated interventions and assessments for children and individuals with mental health disorders

OT403.title: Lower Extremity Rehabilitation
OT403.description: Students will explore the occupational therapy process, covering assessment, intervention, and evaluation of outcomes. The course includes practical lab sessions where students will practice therapeutic techniques and use various tools. It addresses the entire OT process, from referral to discharge, emphasizing the design of patient-centered and sustainable intervention plans, and the application of innovative techniques in simulated clinical settings. Students will assess the effectiveness of interventions based on client progress and work collaboratively to enhance their skills, adaptability, and decision- making. Ethical considerations, professional standards, and innovative approaches to ensure sustainable healthcare outcomes are also integral parts of the curriculum

OT405.title: OT for Geriatrics
OT405.description: This course addresses the specialized needs of geriatric clients, emphasizing interventions that promote safety, independence, and sustainable well-being in older adults. Through hands-on practical sessions, students will gain experience in assessing and developing tailored treatment plans for geriatric patients experiencing physical, cognitive, and psychosocial challenges. The course also integrates evidence-based practices, innovative approaches, and ethical principles to enhance quality of life, preserve dignity, and foster resilience in aging. Students will be prepared to meet the complex demands of geriatric care with sensitivity, professionalism, and client-centered strategies

OT406.title: Occupational-Related Disability
OT406.description: This course explores how occupational therapy addresses work- related injuries and occupational disabilities. It provides an overview of medical conditions commonly seen by occupational therapists, including their diagnostic features, associated conditions, prevalence, and course of disease. Students will learn to design occupational therapy interventions for specific impairments, emphasizing evidence-based, innovative, and sustainable practices. The practical component focuses on ergonomic assessments and the development of comprehensive return-to-work plans that promote long-term recovery, workplace safety, and sustainable occupational performance

OT407.title: OT and Healthcare System
OT407.description: This course provides an in-depth understanding of how occupational therapy fits within the broader healthcare system, including its role in interdisciplinary teams, reimbursement models, and healthcare policies. Students will learn to navigate healthcare systems and advocate for OT services. It emphasizes how occupational therapists can influence health policy, advocate for change and address emerging professional ethical issues. The practical component includes real-world case studies where students interact with healthcare systems and address policy issues

OT410.title: Graduation Project
OT410.description: In this capstone course, students design and complete a research or practice-based project that addresses a real-world issue in occupational therapy. Under faculty guidance, students apply research methodologies and present their findings to peers and professionals. The course covers the overall research design and implementation process while developing skills needed for publication, dissemination, and presentation. Emphasis is placed on evidence-based, innovative, and sustainable practices that strengthen the relevance and impact of occupational therapy research. The course also involves hands-on data collection and analysis, ensuring projects are grounded in rigorous, practice- oriented evidence

OT411.title: Clinical Practice (CP)-I
OT411.description: This course provides students with practical experience in real- world clinical settings, enabling them to apply theoretical knowledge to direct patient care under the supervision of trained specialists. Students will actively participate in evaluating, diagnosing, and managing neurological, pediatric, psychiatric, geriatric, and musculoskeletal disorders. They will develop proficiency in applying advanced occupational therapy methods, therapeutic exercises, and manual treatment techniques to improve patient outcomes. The course emphasizes effective patient communication, infection prevention and control, and the integration of evidence-based, innovative practices into clinical decision- making. Students will collaborate with multidisciplinary healthcare teams to ensure ethical practice and professional communication. Additionally, they will gain expertise in patient education, including self-management techniques, injury prevention, and sustainable home exercise regimens that promote long-term recovery and independence

OT412.title: Clinical Practice (CP)-II
OT412.description: This course provides students with hands-on experience in real- world clinical settings, enabling them to apply theoretical knowledge gained throughout the program to direct patient care. Students will take an active role in the assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of musculoskeletal, neurological, pediatric, psychiatric, and geriatric conditions. They will gain proficiency in applying manual treatment techniques, therapeutic exercises, and advanced occupational therapy procedures to enhance patient outcomes. Emphasis is placed on professional communication, ethical decision-making, and collaboration with interdisciplinary healthcare teams. Students will also develop expertise in patient education, focusing on injury prevention, self-management strategies, and sustainable home exercise regimens that support long-term healing, recovery, and independence

OT413.title: Clinical Practice (CP)-III
OT413.description: This course is designed to enhance the clinical skills and knowledge of occupational therapy students, preparing them for advanced practice in diverse healthcare settings. Through a blend of theoretical instruction, hands-on practice, and reflective learning, students will deepen their understanding of complex clinical scenarios and develop the competencies required for high-level professional practice. Students will actively participate in the evaluation, diagnosis, and management of neurological, pediatric, psychiatric, geriatric, and musculoskeletal disorders. They will build proficiency in applying advanced occupational therapy methods, therapeutic exercises, and manual treatment techniques to improve patient outcomes. The course emphasizes advanced skills, evidence-based therapies, and specialized knowledge essential for complex patient care. Students will gain experience with innovative evaluation methods, customized treatment plans, and creative therapeutic approaches tailored to diverse demographics. A focus is placed on addressing physical, cognitive, and psychosocial challenges by integrating theoretical frameworks, advanced clinical reasoning, and sustainable modern techniques that promote long-term recovery and independence

OT414.title: Clinical Practice (CP)-IV
OT414.description: This course is designed to advance the clinical skills and knowledge of occupational therapy students, preparing them for high-level practice in diverse healthcare settings. Through a combination of theoretical instruction, hands-on practice, and reflective learning, students will deepen their understanding of complex clinical scenarios and develop the competencies required for specialized and sustainable professional practice. Students will actively participate in the evaluation, diagnosis, and management of neurological, pediatric, psychiatric, geriatric, and musculoskeletal disorders. They will gain proficiency in applying advanced occupational therapy methods, therapeutic exercises, and manual treatment techniques to optimize patient outcomes. With an emphasis on advanced skills, evidence-based therapies, and specialized knowledge for complex patient care, the course equips students with innovative evaluation methods, customized treatment plans, and creative therapeutic approaches for diverse populations. The focus is on addressing physical, cognitive, and psychosocial challenges by integrating theoretical frameworks, advanced clinical reasoning, and sustainable modern techniques that promote long-term recovery and independence. Bachelor Of Science In Physiotherapy

PT301.title: Introduction to Physiotherapy
PT301.description: This course introduces the field of physiotherapy, including its history, core principles, and various specialties. It covers different assessment methods used to assess client’s health beside the critical interventions used. The course also provides an overview of professional roles and responsibilities in the healthcare system

PT304.title: Therapeutic Exercise
PT304.description: This course provides an overview of therapeutic exercises concepts and applications. The theoretical component covers the principles and implementation of exercise interventions tailored to enhance strength, flexibility, endurance, and mobility. The practical component focuses on practicing the skills required for exercise therapy and applying these exercises in a clinical setting, allowing students to create individualized plans that address specific needs for the client

PT305.title: Biomechanics and Kinesiology – 1
PT305.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of biomechanics and kinesiology, focusing on human movement. The theoretical part includes exploring mechanical principles, joint function, and muscle action, while the practical component emphasizes analyzing both normal and pathological movement patterns through hands-on activities. These foundational skills are crucial for developing effective physiotherapy interventions

PT306.title: Physiotherapy for Respiratory Conditions
PT306.description: This course provides students with essential knowledge and skills to assess and manage common respiratory pathologies through physiotherapy interventions. Focusing on conditions affecting respiratory health, students will explore physical manifestations, clinical reasoning, and therapeutic strategies specific to respiratory physiotherapy. Emphasis is placed on developing clinical competency in assessing and treating clients with respiratory disorders, utilizing evidence-based approaches to predict and evaluate treatment outcomes effectively. Topics include physiotherapy management of common respiratory disorders, intensive care unit (ICU) respiratory care, and post- operative respiratory rehabilitation. Additionally, students will learn to design programs for promoting respiratory health and preventing disease recurrence. Through practical training and theoretical instruction, students will gain the skills necessary to address respiratory health challenges in different clinical settings

PT307.title: :Physiotherapy for Cardiovascular Conditions
PT307.description: This course focuses on the physiotherapy treatment of cardiovascular conditions, including coronary artery disease, heart failure, and post-cardiac surgery rehabilitation. The theoretical component covers cardiovascular anatomy, physiology, and exercise prescription, while the practical component involves monitoring patient progress and implementing rehabilitation programs to improve cardiovascular health

PT308.title: Physiotherapy for Musculoskeletal Conditions
PT308.description: This course provides essential knowledge, skills, and competencies for managing musculoskeletal conditions using specialized physiotherapy techniques. Students will explore the physiotherapist’s role in assessing and treating musculoskeletal disorders across all age groups and various stages of care. Emphasis is placed on developing practical skills for identifying, evaluating, and addressing musculoskeletal dysfunctions through evidence-based physiotherapy interventions. Through hands-on practice, students will refine their clinical reasoning in assessing and selecting effective treatment methods. Topics include regional examination processes, differential diagnosis, prognosis, and intervention strategies. By the end of this course, students will be prepared to deliver comprehensive musculoskeletal care across diverse clinical setting

PT309.title: Physiotherapy for Neurological Conditions
PT309.description: This course provides students with essential knowledge and skills for managing neurological conditions through specialized physiotherapy interventions. Students will gain an understanding of common neurological pathologies, their physical manifestations, and the clinical reasoning processes involved in assessing, diagnosing, and treating neurological disorders. Emphasis is placed on developing practical and communication skills necessary for the safe and effective treatment of clients with neurological impairments. Topics include evidence-based treatment approaches, such as Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF), Motor Relearning Program (MRP), and other techniques designed to enhance coordination and balance. The course also covers strategies for promoting neurological health and preventing disease recurrence, equipping students with a comprehensive approach to neurological physiotherapy across diverse clinical settings

PT310.title: Physiotherapy for Pediatrics
PT310.description: Physiotherapy for Pediatrics is a specialized course aimed at providing students with essential knowledge, skills, and clinical reasoning to effectively assess and manage pediatric patients with diverse physical and developmental conditions. The theoretical component covers pediatric conditions such as cerebral palsy and developmental delays, while the practical part involves age-appropriate assessment and intervention techniques, including play-based therapy to enhance motor skills and functional abilities in children

PT311.title: Physiotherapy for Geriatrics
PT311.description: This course focuses on physiotherapy for older adults, addressing common geriatric conditions like arthritis, osteoporosis, and balance disorders. The theoretical component covers assessment and management strategies, while the practical component emphasizes promoting mobility, independence, and fall prevention through hands-on interventions

PT312.title: Physiotherapy for Obstetrics and Gynecology
PT312.description: This course covers physiotherapy in the context of obstetric and gynecological health. The theoretical component includes conditions like pelvic floor dysfunction and prenatal care, while the practical part focuses on hands-on techniques for pain management, improving physical health during pregnancy, and patient education

PT401.title: Orthotics and Prosthetics
PT401.description: This course introduces students to the principles of orthotics and prosthetics in rehabilitation. The theoretical component covers design and fitting, while the practical component involves assessing patients and integrating orthoses and prostheses into treatment plans to enhance mobility and independence

PT402.title: Biomechanics and Kinesiology – 2
PT402.description: Building on the concepts from Biomechanics and Kinesiology - 1, this course delves into advanced aspects of human movement. The theoretical component covers pathological movement patterns and joint mechanics, while the practical component involves applying these principles in clinical assessments and rehabilitation strategies

PT404.title: Physiotherapy for Surgical Conditions
PT404.description: This course focuses on physiotherapy interventions for patients undergoing surgery. The theoretical component covers pre- and post-operative care, while the practical component emphasizes hands-on rehabilitation techniques for restoring mobility and function following surgeries like joint replacements and spinal procedures

PT409.title: Sports Physiotherapy
PT409.description: This course covers the principles of sports physiotherapy, including injury prevention, assessment, and rehabilitation. The theoretical component focuses on exercise physiology and biomechanics, while the practical component involves hands-on techniques to help athletes recover safely and enhance performance

PT411.title: Advanced Technology in Physiotherapy (AI and Metaverse)
PT411.description: This course introduces students to emerging technologies in physiotherapy, such as AI and virtual reality. The theoretical component covers the application of these technologies, their limitations, ethical and legal concerns. The practical component involves applying these tools in simulated clinical settings to gain experience thus enhance patient care and rehabilitation outcomes

PT413.title: Graduation Project
PT413.description: In this capstone course, students design and complete a research or practice-based project addressing a real-world issue in physical therapy. Guided by faculty, students apply research methodologies, conduct evidence-based data collection, and present their findings to peers and professionals. The course emphasizes hands-on analysis, ensuring applicability in physical therapy practice

PT414.title: Clinical Practice (CP)-I
PT414.description: This course introduces students to the foundational aspects of practical experience in a clinical setting, focusing on basic skills and supervised applications. Students will begin by learning infection prevention and control, effective patient communication, and basic physiotherapy techniques. Fundamental learning outcomes include patient evaluation, history-taking, and treatment planning based on evidence-based practices. Students will also participate in weekly clinical rotations to integrate classroom learning into real-world scenarios

PT415.title: Clinical Practice (CP)-II
PT415.description: This course equips students with advanced clinical skills, focusing on manual therapy techniques, advanced physiotherapy modalities, and collaboration with orthopedic specialists. Students will enhance their ability to design individualized rehabilitation programs, monitor patient progress, and incorporate cutting-edge technologies like electrotherapy and therapeutic ultrasound into treatment plans. The course also emphasizes advanced patient education strategies, including injury prevention and self-management, alongside ethical decision-making in multidisciplinary teams to ensure comprehensive, professional patient care

PT416.title: Clinical Practice (CP)-III
PT416.description: This course offers advanced, practical instruction in a supervised clinical environment, enabling students to implement theoretical knowledge in actual patient care. The focus is on assessing, diagnosing, and managing musculoskeletal, sports, and muscle injuries, along with disorders in obstetrics, gynecology, pediatrics, and geriatrics. Students will utilize advanced physiotherapy techniques, including manual treatment and therapeutic exercises, to enhance patient outcomes and learn evidence-based procedures. The training emphasizes patient education, self-management, injury avoidance, and home rehabilitation approaches for enduring recovery

PT417.title: Clinical Practice (CP)-IV
PT417.description: This course offers advanced, practical instruction in a supervised clinical environment, allowing students to implement theoretical knowledge in actual patient care. The course focuses on assessing, diagnosing, and managing musculoskeletal, sports, and muscle injuries, along with disorders in obstetrics, gynecology, pediatrics, and geriatrics. Students will utilize advanced physiotherapy techniques, including manual treatment and therapeutic exercises, to enhance patient outcomes and learn evidence-based procedures. Essential elements encompass enhancing communication abilities to cultivate empathy and professionalism, engaging with interdisciplinary teams for ethical decision-making, and executing patient-centered care methodologies. The training emphasizes patient education, self-management, injury avoidance, and home rehabilitation approaches for enduring recovery. Students will refine their ability to adapt and optimize treatment strategies through comprehensive patient assessments, effective treatment planning, and leveraging advanced physiotherapy technologies. Under the guidance of orthopedic specialists, participants will refine their abilities in tracking progress and modifying interventions. Evaluations, including weekly clinical case presentations, Objective-Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCE), and Objective-Structured Practical Examinations (OSPE), will assess the student's practical and clinical competencies. Upon completing the course, students will possess the skills to provide safe, effective, patient-centered care in various physiotherapy environments, prepared for professional practice. Diploma in Health Management and Informatics

RCM220.title: Cardiopulmonary Anatomy and Physiology
RCM220.description: This course provides core knowledge of the normal structure and function of the anatomy and physiology of the cardiopulmonary system. The structures and functions of this system will provide a foundation for studies in airway management, respiratory diseases, pulmonary function testing and human physiology, which deal with acid-base, blood gas disturbances and interpretation. Study units will include topics on respiratory system, thoracic cavity, cardiovascular, mechanics of ventilation, gas exchange and transport and pulmonary diffusion of gases. Clinical application of common anatomical principles will be discussed in this course

RCM221.title: Introduction to Respiratory Care Profession
RCM221.description: This course provides an introduction to the profession of respiratory care with emphasis on the duties, responsibilities, respiratory organizations, historical development of this filed and qualifications of a respiratory therapist. Elementary lung disease processes and basic knowledge on respiratory equipment are also described

RCM310.title: Respiratory Care Science I
RCM310.description: This course provides the students an introduction to the clinical sciences related to the profession of respiratory care. The course will cover, in detail, the basic principles of gasses, and the clinical use of medical gases (Oxygen, Nitric Oxide, Heliox), humidity and aerosol therapy. Emphasis will be placed on the physical and chemical principles, which influence therapeutic modalities

RCM311.title: Patient Assessment
RCM311.description: This course introduces students to the techniques used in the diagnosis of cardiopulmonary diseases. This course involves a systematic study of bedside assessment, patient history, signs, symptoms, thoracic imaging, laboratory techniques and results, electrocardiograph all of which serve as a foundation for clinical assessment and diagnosis. Other diagnostic techniques which are commonly performed or analyzed by the Respiratory Therapist

RCM320.title: Cardiopulmonary Disease I
RCM320.description: The course is to provide students with specific knowledge of cardiopulmonary diseases, which affect ventilation, gas diffusion and respiration. The Course will cover topics of general respiratory pathophysiology, such as obstructive and restrictive lung disease and others. Subsequent topics will concentrate on specific diseases, including their clinical presentation, etiology, diagnosis and management. Knowledge of these diseases, along with an understanding of the function of the normal lung, will provide a foundation for the rational application of therapeutic modalities

RCM321.title: Fundamentals of Polysomnography
RCM321.description: This course introduces the students to the physiology of the normal sleep cycle, the clinical assessment of sleepiness, the classifications of sleep disorders and other forms of treatment of sleep disorders. This course also focuses during the laboratory sessions on scoring of polysomnography tracings, applying of therapeutic interventions such titration of CPAP/Bi-Level therapy, and patient education

RCM322.title: Mechanical Ventilation I
RCM322.description: This course is designed to provide students with introductory concepts of mechanical ventilation, such as classification, modes of mechanical ventilation, settings, indication and complications. Basic understanding of the most commonly used ventilators and their clinical application is also covered

RCM323.title: Respiratory Care Science II
RCM323.description: This course introduces students to airway management, lung expansion therapy and airway clearance therapy, topics essential in the practice of respiratory care. The course involves study units in the anatomy of the airways, artificial airways and guidelines for airway management, maintenance of airways, methods of tracheobronchial hygiene and lung expansion therapy. The course will also prepare students for procedures such as arterial and capillary punctures

RCM324.title: Respiratory Care Clinical Practice I
RCM324.description: This field course provides entry-level clinical experience. Topics include basic life support, universal precautions, patient safety, patient’s medical record, communication, infection control, medical gas systems and oxygen, humidity and aerosol delivery devices, airway management, lung expansion therapy, tracheobronchial hygiene, and arterial punctures and sampling. The field course also covers basics of mechanical ventilation

RCM410.title: Mechanical Ventilation II
RCM410.description: This course is a continuation to the course: Basic Mechanical Ventilation, with emphasis on advanced modes used in mechanical ventilation of various disease states, neonatal, home care, transportation and long-term ventilation. The course also puts emphasis on management strategies of mechanical ventilation according to disease entities

RCM411.title: Respiratory Care Clinical Practice II
RCM411.description: This clinical field course is designed to provide clinical experience and patients’ outcome evaluation related to delivery of airway pharmacology, transportation of critically ill patients and basic mechanical ventilation, with emphasis on advanced modes, ventilator graphics and management strategies used in mechanical ventilation of various disease

RCM412.title: Patient Care Management Seminar
RCM412.description: This seminar provides the student with an opportunity to integrate and to present the medical management related to patients who have cardiopulmonary disorders. Students meet with an instructor to present a patient admission scenario, including the patient history, examination, evaluation, diagnosis, prognosis, and intervention as well as objective determination of success of intervention. Emphasis will be placed on decision making and problem solving as they relate to respiratory care

RCM413.title: Cardiopulmonary Disease II
RCM413.description: This course is a continuation to the course: cardiopulmonary diseases I (RCM 320). The course is to provide students with specific knowledge of cardiopulmonary disorders and related conditions, which affect ventilation, gas diffusion and respiration. Knowledge of these disorders and conditions, along with an understanding for their clinical presentation, etiology and diagnosis, will provide a foundation for the rational application of therapeutic modalities

RCM414.title: Pulmonary Function Diagnostics
RCM414.description: The course is to introduce students to the methodologies and physiological importance of specialized, diagnostic tests, which are performed in the pulmonary function laboratory. The Course will cover techniques used to gather physiological data, comparing it to normal populations, interpreting and translating this information into a descriptive, diagnostic presentation. Diseases that commonly require pulmonary function tests are described. Bronchodilator studies to determine reversibility of airway obstruction are also presented. The course will cover the principles of measurement of Spirometry, indirect measurement of lung volumes with gas dilution techniques and body plethysmography. It also describes the measurement of pulmonary diffusing capacity using small volumes of carbon monoxide (DLCO) and diagnosis of bronchial hyper- responsiveness in patients with normal spirometry and cardiopulmonary exercise

RCM420.title: Multidisciplinary Respiratory Care
RCM420.description: This course is designed to cover three essential areas in respiratory and critical care practice: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation, Trauma and Advanced Radiology. These areas need specialized knowledge and in-depth skills to prepare students to the level of advanced standards due to the recent vast development in global health care

RCM421.title: Pulmonary Rehabilitation and Home Care
RCM421.description: This course provides the knowledge and comprehension of pulmonary rehabilitation, in patients with limiting respiratory conditions in order to improve patients' exercise tolerance and quality of life and reduce breathlessness. It covers patient education and caregiver to maintain the highest possible functional capacity to patients. Topics are: medication regimens, smoking cession, breathing retaining, bronchial hygiene, special equipment set-up and servicing, patient and family education, patient evaluation. This course will also address the respiratory care home care services in terms of procedure, equipment and modalities

RCM422.title: Pediatric Respiratory Care
RCM422.description: This course is designed to cover major aspects of pediatric respiratory care. The course involves the topics about assessment of the child, details of respiratory disorders, cardiovascular disorders and about the acutely ill child. This course will also deal with pediatric advanced life support and management of the pediatric on mechanical ventilator

RCM423.title: Respiratory Care Clinical Practice III
RCM423.description: This clinical practice course provides advanced field experience in respiratory care with a focus on the management, monitoring, and transport of mechanically ventilated patients, as well as long-term respiratory care planning. Emphasis is placed on interpreting ventilator waveforms, hemodynamic data, and implementing evidence-based strategies for patient management in critical care settings. The course also includes clinical exposure to chronic cardiopulmonary care, incorporating discharge planning, rehabilitation, home ventilation, and supportive services. Students will gain hands-on experience in both acute and long-term care facilities, supporting the development of advanced clinical decision-making skills. The course aligns with Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 3 (Good Health and Well-being) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities), promoting equitable, high-quality respiratory care across diverse healthcare settings

RCM424.title: Neonatal Respiratory Care
RCM424.description: This course is designed to cover major aspects of neonatal respiratory care. The course involves the topics about fetal lung development, fetal circulation, and transition to extrauterine life it also deals with topics about assessment of the neonate, respiratory disorders, cardiovascular disorders. This course will also deal with neonatal resuscitation guidelines and management of the pediatric on mechanical ventilator

RCM510.description: This seminar course provides simulated practice and scenarios of patient care skills in a multimedia setting. It allows students to cover clinical simulation of different patient scenarios related to respiratory care which requires specialized knowledge in solving patient management problems written in a branching logic format. Simulation and role playing of various clinical situations in the lab will enhance the classroom experience and skills

RCM511.title: Essentials of Critical Care
RCM511.description: This course provides the students with core knowledge and skills with different essential monitoring and diagnostic techniques and modalities for critically ill patients in the critical care setting. These include procedures, such, fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, hemodynamic monitoring, bronchoscopy, pleural interventions (chest tube & pleural aspiration) and cardiac outputs

RCM512.title: Respiratory Care Seminar
RCM512.description: This seminar course is to discuss specialty topics selected by instructor and students. This course will also offer to students advanced topics presented by specialists- Pulmonologist, Intensivist, neonatologist, Internist, Respiratory Therapists and other medical specialists. This course is to have students discuss, evaluate and gain knowledge from presenting and attending many case studies related mainly on perinatal & pediatric topics, sleep disorders and rehabilitation and home care

RCM513.title: Graduation Project
RCM513.description: This course provides students with the opportunity to apply research skills and carry out a research project related to the major program under the supervision of a faculty member. Students will be required to conduct literature review and perform data collection, statistical analysis, writing up of the research paper. Students participating in research must complete CITI program (https://about.citiprogram.org/en/homepage/) for research ethics and compliance training prior to submitting research proposals

RCM520.title: Respiratory Care Clinical Practice IV
RCM520.description: This clinical practice course provides a capstone advanced clinical field experience. The clinical time will allow the student to continue their hands-on clinical learning. Emphasis is on respiratory care therapeutic and diagnostic patient care for critically ill patients in different settings. These include procedures, such as hemodynamic monitoring, ECG interpretation, fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, bronchoscopy, pleural interventions in vivo blood gas monitoring and management of trauma and post-cardiothoracic surgical care. Bachelor of Science in Medical Diagnostic Imaging Core Major Courses

THM301.title: Introduction to Hospitality Management
THM301.description: The course focuses on hospitality operations while offering a broad, comprehensive view of Hospitality Industry. It provides an understanding of hospitality and Tourism industry major aspects and its operational aspects. The course is structured in areas of Hospitality and lodging, Tourism attractions, Recreations, and Events and its operations. The purpose of the course is to enable students explore the workings of hospitality segment, including hospitality and lodging; beverages, restaurants, and managed services; tourism, recreation, attractions, clubs, and gaming; assemblies, events, and attractions; and managerial areas of the hospitality industry

THM302.title: Tourism Management and Development
THM302.description: The course traces the history and evolution of tourism concerning the changing tourism demand and travel motivations over some time. The course also provides valuable information on tourism sector components and linkages with accommodation, transportation, and tour operators. Special focus is laid on visitor attractions and events. As a foundation course, this course introduces participants to the fundamentals of tourism with a global focus. The students will be enlightened on the need of developing and managing tourism with a focus on the role of the private and public sectors in effectively managing the resources

THM311.title: Tourism and hospitality marketing
THM311.description: The goal of the course is to help students comprehend marketing management from a tourism perspective. The course focuses on the methods and techniques through which tourism organizations examine and evaluate marketing trends. The course also covers defining and choosing target markets, planning and executing marketing strategies, and implementing marketing control plans. Students will develop the skills to analyze and address marketing challenges and opportunities in tourism products, services, and destinations. They will also understand the components that make tourism marketing successful and gain both the theoretical and practical skills necessary for success

THM400.title: Business Economics in Tourism and Hospitality
THM400.description: This course provides necessary skills and knowledge of Business Economics in Tourism and Hospitality through a comprehensive analysis of the market forces, demand and supply, firm behavior & strategy, and transaction and institution

THM401.title: Event management
THM401.description: The purpose of the course is to make students understand the significance of events in developing and promoting tourism. This course focuses on the theories and practices of conceiving and organizing successful events. The course contents include event design and management, outcomes, event experiences and their associated meanings, dynamic processes shaping events, and why people attend them. The course introduces the functional and operational aspects of event management, emphasizing cultural and heritage events and sustainability. They will learn how to derive tourism potential of a destination through events and festivals

THM410.title: Operation Planning and Scheduling
THM410.description: This course equips students with essential skills, and techniques for the operation management in the service industry with an emphasis of hospitability industry. The course is designed to provide knowledge regarding the structure of decision-making and organizational management of a service with an emphasis on technical methods in forecasting, inventory management, material requirement planning and operations scheduling. The purpose of the course is to develop the ability to apply analytical and managerial methods for the management of a service. It includes techniques based on forecasting, supply chain, organization and MRP applications, quality evaluation and continuous improvement methods. The student will be able to manage, evaluate and monitor different aspects of the service industry

THM411.title: Information Technology in Tourism
THM411.description: The course examines the challenges of using information technology in the tourism business. The contents cover IT applications in various industries, such as airlines, travel intermediates, lodging, food service, destinations, attractions, events, and entertainment. With the help of examples and cases, the course examines how travelers use technology for decision- making before, during, and after their trip. This course aims to offer thorough range of important trends, opportunities, and issues in hotel and travel information technology. The students will have the chance to learn about novel topics like big data, robotics, crowdsourcing for sustainability, intelligent destinations, disruptive innovation, and augmented and virtual reality

THM412.title: Tour Leadership and Management
THM412.description: The course aims to equip students with relevant knowledge and skills, enabling them to perform functions and operations of tour management successfully. The students will learn the essentials of tour management, including pre-tour, on-tour, and post-tour operations. The course will follow a practice-oriented approach focusing on tour management and guiding, such as planning tour itineraries, handling large groups manage cultural differences, grievances, emergencies, and such. The contents will also cover a tour manager’s responsibilities towards tourists, destinations, and other tourism stakeholders

THM415.title: Graduation Project
THM415.description: This course provides an opportunity for students to employ academic tools and analysis techniques to research a project that is directly relevant to their majors and their future career. This course can be offered as a 3-credit hour course for students who wish to pursue only the classroom portion of this course and a 6-credit hour course for those who wish to combine research with an internship. The Graduation Project will include weekly classroom sessions for all students to engage in discussions related to idea generation, research techniques and data analysis. Students will also be required to attend several smaller group sessions in which they present their ideas and progress and receive feedback. Students may work individually or in teams and must deliver a case study or paper at the end of the course

THM419.title: Internship
THM419.description: The course consists of 200 hours of work in a private or public organization. The student may select to have his/her internship in any area of business administration or information technology. The choice of workplace is subject to the approval of LCT

THM421.title: Financial Accounting in Hospitality
THM421.description: This course demonstrates and explains the significance of financial management aspects within the hotel and tourism businesses and provides many examples and is mainly based on practical implementation more than the theoretical aspects. The main purpose for this course is to discuss the following: The concept of Relationship Between Return and Risk; the concept of purchasing power of money and time value of money; Financial assets with Fixed Income such as preferred stock & bonds; Common equity; Cost of Capital; Capital Budgeting and Cash Flow Estimation and Capital Budgeting Decision approaches for those in hotel and tourism professions

THM422.title: Managing sustainable tourism
THM422.description: The purpose of the course is to introduce students to a range of crucial topics such as mass tourism, alternative tourism, human capital management, and sustainable development. The course bridges the gap between theoretical perspectives of sustainable tourism and their application in the commercial and non- commercial arena; this course facilitates comprehensive learning of sustainable tourism development. The course provides a comprehensive introduction to sustainable tourism, crucially combining theoretical and practical approaches to successfully equip students with the tools to manage a sustainable tourism business or destination.
